Ethos Proxy Get fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation to get an Ethos resource through Ethos Integration.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example persons.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

When selecting the GET method in the API Selector, if there are multiple GET methods displayed, select the method with the path that does not include {id}.

After you select the resource, the resource you selected and the version you selected are populated on the Ethos Proxy Get fitting page.

If you select a major or minor version, the major version is automatically populated, so that the user is pinned to the floating major version. If the user selects a patch version, the specific patch version is populated in Data Connect.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Accept Versions

Required. List of supported resource version numbers. Each version will be tried in order until a response code of 406 is not returned. Up to 10 versions can be specified; additional versions will be ignored.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.

You can enter in multiple accept versions in the fittings. However, you can not select multiple versions from the API Selector. You can still manually type in additional API versions.
Alternative Representation Optional. Alternative representation
Id from Payload Optional. JSONPath to id within payload itself. Mutually exclusive from Id from Context. Ex. "$.person.id".
Id from Context Optional. JSONPath to id within context. Mutually exclusive from Id from Payload, for example "$.guid".
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put Ethos response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload.
Result Headers Optional. Dot-notation target within message to put response headers. When not set headers will be dropped silently. Valid examples: theHeaders, payload.theHeaders, header.theHeaders, message.payload.theHeaders, message.header.theHeaders. Note that if the response is an array, the headers will be saved into message.header.propName even if payload was specified as the place to save them. Repeated headers will be stored in an array value.
Cache Optional. Flag to enabled or disable response caching, defaults to false. When successful, the response will be cached using the resource or resource + id used. Cached information will expire after one hour. Please note that the cache can be populated or retrieved by other pipelines using the matching resource, resource id and method (GET).
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error".
Api Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter, which will contain the the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.

Example

The following is an example of how to use Ethos Proxy Get:

  1. In order for this fitting to work, an Ethos API Key should be created as a parameter. Click the drop-down menu aside the pipeline name, select Edit Pipeline Settings, and add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the fitting configuration.
  2. Enter the following fitting configuration:
    • Fitting Name: Ethos Proxy Get
    • Resource: persons (in lowercase)
    • Accept Versions: 12
    • Get Id From: Context
    • Id From Context: $.personGuid
  3. For this example, an optional string pipeline parameter named personGuid will be defined. This parameter is going to be used by the fitting as the ID of the person.
  4. Run the test. Use a valid Ethos API Key and the persons GUID or ID. This will retrieve the information of the person with the specified ID.

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that is the response. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

If neither the idFromPayload nor the idFromContext properties are specified the resource is queried without ID as a get all. The same happens if the personGuid value is not provided.

When specifying the idFromPayload or idFromContext configuration properties but provided with a JSONPath syntax that is not valid, the Ethos resource isn't reached, the original input message passes along to the next fitting and an error gets reported.

Ethos Proxy Get Array fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation to get an Ethos array of resources through Ethos Integration.

This fitting only supports an array for a single resource, such as an array of addresses. The intended use is not to get an array of different Ethos resources.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object containing an array of an Ethos resource.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example, addresses.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

When selecting the GET method in the API Selector, if there are multiple GET methods displayed, select the method with the path that does not include {id}.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Accept Versions

Required. List of supported resource version numbers.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.

You can enter in multiple accept versions in the fittings. However, you can not select multiple versions from the API Selector. You can still manually type in additional API versions.
Alternative Representation Optional. Alternative representation.
Id from Payload Optional. JSONPath to id list within payload itself, for example, $.person.addresses[*].address.id.
Json Path Target Required. JSONPath target within payload to put Ethos response, for example, $.person.addresses[*].address.
Response Id Field Optional. Property name from response to compare for target replacement, defaults to "id".
Cache Optional. Flag to enabled or disable response caching, defaults to false.
Ignore Errors Optional. flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error".
Api Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.

Example

The following is an example of how to use Ethos Proxy Get Array

  1. In order for this fitting to work, an Ethos Api Key should be created as a parameter. Click the drop-down menu aside the pipeline name, select Edit Pipeline Settings, and add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the Api Key in the configuration.
  2. Enter the following configuration:
    • Resource: persons
    • Enter Accept Versions: 12. Click the + button after entering this parameter.
    • Id From Payload: $.persons[*].person.id
    • Json Path Target: $.persons[*].person
  3. The input should contain IDs for persons. The input data should have a JSON that looks like this:
    {
  "persons": [
    {
      "person": {
        "id": "invalid-id"
      }
    },
    {
      "person": {
        "id": "268a03c6-56c7-462f-8479-d4ebb07984ad"
      }
    }
    ,
    {
      "person": {
        "id": "989b7725-a875-44b8-9195-e67b09bd1b3f"
      }
    }
  ]
}

Response is returned for that resource matching (by ID) the first item in the persons array in the payload, and inserting the response replacing that ID with the response payload. The unmatched ID remains unchanged.

Ethos Proxy Get With Filter fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation to get an Ethos array of resources through Ethos Integration with optional filter criteria. The filter criteria is specified in the URL of the request and is usually some ID (GUID) value.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object containing some data in the message payload used by the criteria filter.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example persons.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

When selecting the GET method in the API Selector, if there are multiple GET methods displayed, select the method with the path that does not include {id}.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Filter Optional. Querystring criteria to be used along specified resource. It can contain mustache type reference tags, for example, ?criteria={"id":"{{person.id}}"}

Because Mustache and JSON path share some similarities, the format to use can cause some confusion. See Common questions.
Page Size

Optional. Limits the result set size, for example 10.

Page size determines the number of records returned per page. Data Connect retrieves all pages with pagination.

If you want to limit the total number of records to be retrieved, include a limit as part of the criteria. For example, ?limit=100&criteria={…}
Payload Target Path Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put Ethos response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload, for example person.results.
Result Headers Optional. Dot-notation target within message to put response headers. When not set headers will be dropped silently. Valid examples: theHeaders, payload.theHeaders, header.theHeaders, message.payload.theHeaders, message.header.theHeaders. Note that if the response is an array, the headers will be saved into message.header.propName even if payload was specified as the place to save them. Repeated headers will be stored in an array value.
Accept Versions

Required. List of supported resource version numbers.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.

You can enter in multiple accept versions in the fittings. However, you can not select multiple versions from the API Selector. You can still manually type in additional API versions.
Alternative Representation Optional. Alternative representation.
Cache Optional. Flag to enabled or disable response caching, defaults to false.
Query By Post Optional. If set, the URL will be /qapi instead of /api, and any filter configuration will be ignored.

When a QAPI is selected from the API selector, the Query by Post toggle will be set to true.
Content Version

Required. If queryByPost is set. Version for Ethos Resource, for example 12. Ignored otherwise.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.
Body Path Optional. Used if queryByPost is true. A JSON path in the payload which will be used as the body of the post. If set but the path returns undefined, no operation will be done and message will be pushed through.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
ErrorPath Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error".
Api Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.

Example

The following is an example of how to use Ethos proxy Get with filter:

  1. In order for this fitting to work, an Ethos API Key should be created as a parameter. Click the drop-down menu aside the pipeline name, select Edit Pipeline Settings, and add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the fitting configuration.
  2. Enter the following fitting configuration:
    • Resource: persons
    • Filter: ?criteria={"names":[{"firstName":"james"}]}
    • Accept Versions: 12, Click the + button after entering this parameter.
  3. Run the test. This retrieves all the persons that match with the given filter criteria.

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload containing the response. This fitting supports paging. This fitting will determine if paging is needed based on the x-total-count response header, the page size (if specified), and the response body length.

With Paging

If paging is needed, and the payload target path is specified, then the paged response(s) will be concatenated into an array and the array will be inserted into the message payload at the location specified by the payloadTargetPath property in the fitting configuration. The message will then be pushed through this fitting. It should be understood that the payloadTargetPath property is not intended to be used with a high volume of data from many paged responses to prevent running out of memory.

If the payloadTargetPath is not specified, then each paged response will be pushed through this fitting as a separate message.

The page size can also be specified in the fitting configuration. Each paging request will use a limit criteria equal to the page size. If the page size is not specified, the default page size for the given resource as determined by the Ethos resource API is used.

Without Paging

If paging is not needed and the payloadTargetPath configuration property is specified, the response will be inserted into the message payload at the location specified by the payloadTargetPath, and the message will be pushed through this fitting.

If paging is not needed and the payloadTargetPath is not specified, then the response will replace the message payload, and the message will be pushed through this fitting.

Query by Post

To use an Ethos QAPI endpoint, set queryByPost to true and also specify contentVersion. The payload of the message coming into this fitting becomes the body of the outgoing QAPI call. Paging is supported on the QAPI response.

File List (AWS S3 List Objects) fitting

Use this fitting to retrieve a list of file names stored in S3.

Expected input

No input is required but message payload should preferably be of type object. Message is only required if the filePrefix has message dependent interpolation references.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
File Prefix Required. Case-sensitive, retrieves only the files with the given prefix.
Target Optional. Payload target. Supports dot-notation structure.
Bucket Optional. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an S3 bucket name.
Access Key Id Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Access Key ID.
Secret Access Key Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Secret Key.

Key Interpolation

The config.filePrefix allows for interpolation tags that take into account values in context and processed message (including header and payload).

Some examples of filePrefix values:

  • Roster - Simple hardcoded value (no interpolation).
  • {{context.filePrefix}} - Interpolated value from context
  • {{message.header.filePrefix}} - Interpolated value from message.header
  • {{message.payload.filePrefix}} - Interpolated value from message.payload
  • subfolder/{{context.filePrefix}} - Combination of hardcoded folder with interpolated filename from context
  • {{context.foldername}}/{{message.payload.filePrefix}} - Combination of two interpolated values from both context and message.payload.

The final filePrefix value will always be prefixed by the tenant ID found in pipeline context.

Example

The following is an example of how to use File List

File prefix is the only required parameter. For this example, the File Prefix used will be person.

Expected output

This fitting will retrieve the list of files that matches with the provided text or empty if nothing found.

When config.target is not configured, the result will be set as the outgoing message payload.

When config.target is configured, the process will embed the result in the target's location. If the incoming message is not an instance of message or its payload and not of type object, the original value will be stored in the outgoing message payload's _originalValue property, while the result is placed in the target's location.

Error Handling

Errors while accessing an Object's HEAD metadata will not cause pipeline interruptions. In these cases, the incoming message as-is will be passed through and the error will be reported.

File Reader fitting

Use this fitting to read a file from Ellucian cloud storage, which by default is an Ellucian-maintained AWS S3 bucket.

To specify a bucket of your choosing, use the bucket configuration property and include AWS credentials in the related properties.

Expected input

The fitting accepts, but does not require, a message payload. Either the config.key or the payload's s3.object.key need to be present for the File Reader to work as expected. When both are present, the message payload will take precedence.

Configuration Description
Key Optional. S3 object key. If not provided, message payload needs to specify S3.object.key
Bucket Optional. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an S3 bucket name.
Access Key Id Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Access Key ID.
Secret Access Key Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Secret Key.
Binary Optional: Enables users to define the file transfer mode as binary instead of string.
Error If No File Optional. Flag to generate an error (instead of a warning) if a file is not found on S3.
Allow Concurrent Optional: If set, allows multiple threads to read files concurrently for each input message.

Key Interpolation

The config.key and payload's s3.object.key both accept interpolation tags that will take into account values in context and processed message (including header and payload).

Some examples of key values:

  • sample-file.txt - Simple hardcoded value (no interpolation).
  • {{context.filename}} - Interpolated value from context
  • {{message.header.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.header
  • {{message.payload.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.payload
  • sample-folder/{{context.filename}} - Combination of hardcoded folder with interpolated filename from context
  • {{context.foldername}}/{{message.payload.filename}} - Combination of two interpolated values from both context and message.payload

Example

Following is an example of how to use File Reader

  1. The file reader only needs the key of a file that exists in S3. In the File List example, a list of files with the prefix person was retrieved. One of those is named persons-id-10.txt and contains a list of 10 person IDs. Use persons-ids-10.txt as Key.
  2. After running the example, the content of the file will be retrieved in the payload.

Output

As the fitting receives chunks from S3, they will be pushed as new messages into the pipeline. Each will have the original header from the incoming message, and the payload will be the chunk of data that S3 sent as a string.

HTTP Request fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation.

If your Integration pipeline uses the HTTP fitting to call a custom API that is hosted on-premise only, not through Ethos Integration, your firewall rules should allow for inbound requests from a list of static IP addresses. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected input

A message payload that is a string or JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Method Optional. HTTP method (GET|POST|PUT|DELETE, etc .). Defaults to GET.
Uri Required. Path to the requested resource. for example, http://domain/path.
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put response body
Result Headers Optional. Dot-notation target within message to put response headers. When not set headers will be dropped silently. Valid examples: theHeaders, payload.theHeaders, header.theHeaders, message.payload.theHeaders, message.header.theHeaders. Note that if the response is an array, the headers will be saved into message.header.propName even if payload was specified as the place to save them. Repeated headers will be stored in an array value.
Cache Optional. Flag to enable or disable response caching (only for GET requests), defaults to false.
Stream Optional. Flag to enable or disable response streaming (only for GET requests). When streaming is enabled cache and target will not be supported and result headers are ignored.
Authorization Optional. Authorization specification. The authorization section allows someone to setup user name and password for basic authorization header setup. This will override any explicit authorization header specification at the headers section.
Headers Optional. Hash of key or value pairs to be sent as headers.
Body Optional. Body specifications.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos whenever an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling logic further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.

The uri, method, headers, body.content, authorization.username, and authorization.password configuration fields can be templated using Mustache, with properties from context, message.header, or message.payload.

The authorization section allows someone to setup username and password for basic authorization header setup. This will override any explicit authorization header specification at the headers section.

Ellucian recommends that interpolation is utilized in both username and password. We use mustache.js to interpolate values. Avoid hard coding sensitive access information in a pipeline's configuration.

Example

The following is an example of how to use HTTP request fitting to make OAuth calls with client-id and secret-key.

  1. Enter the following parameters:

    a.

    • Name: clientId
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Client ID
    • Required: Yes
    • Sensitive: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1

    b.

    • Name: clientSecret
    • Required: Yes
    • Sensitive: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1

    c.

    • Name: authUrl
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Authentication URL
    • Required: Yes
    • Type: String

    d.

    • Name: resource
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Resource
    • Required: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1
  2. Enter the following fitting configuration:
    • Fitting Name: getAuthToken
    • Method: POST
    • Uri: {{{context.authUrl}}}
    • Authorization Username: {{{context.clientId}}}
    • Authorization Password: {{{context.clientSecret}}}
    • Body Type: from-urlencoded
    • Body Content: JSON
    {
  "grant_type": "client_credentials",
  "resource": "{{{context.resource}}}"
}

    As shown interpolation with mustache has been used to indicate that the configuration values will be picked up from the parameters during runtime.

  3. Run the test to get the Authorization token from the access_token in the payload of the result. Use the following information in the required fields:
    • Client ID: enterYourClientID
    • Client Secret: enterYourClientSecret
    • Authentication URL: https://test/token
    • Resource: https://testcloud.com

Output

Non-Streamed Requests

By default HTTP Fitting Request response body is read as a whole (in one step) and sent down the pipeline in a message envelope using the same header as the incoming message. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

Streamed Requests

When streaming is enabled by using the stream parameter, the fitting splits the request response body and sends each chunk as it is received down the pipeline as string until all content is read. This is useful for big downloads.

Note:

Result headers are not populated when using the streaming options.

SFTP List fitting

Use this fitting to perform a SFTP list operation to get a list of file names with their size.

If your Integration pipeline uses SFTP fittings, your firewall rules, or the firewall rules of a third party, may need to allow for inbound requests. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Private Key Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the private key used for authentication. This or password must be present. Takes priority over password if defined.
Password Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the password used for authentication. This or privateKey must be present. Ignored if privateKey is defined.
Username Required. Can be interpolated, for example, {{message.payload.username}} or {{context.username}}.
Host Required.
Port Optional. Default is 22. SFTP port supports Mustache expressions.

If the port is a number, use that number.

If the port is a Mustache expression, evaluate it. If it evaluated to a number, use that number instead of the default.

If the value is not a number or a Mustache expression, the value is not valid.
Path Optional. If not provided, the list will be taken from current working directory.
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put response. When not set, it replaces the whole message payload.

Example

The following is an example of how to use SFTP List.

  1. For the SFTP List, when using the private key it is necessary to create a parameter that will contain it, so make sure you have the following when creating SFTP parameter:
    • Create a parameter, for example, sftpKey of type string, with Multi-line enabled.
    • The key should include the comments as well, for example -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- ...etc
  2. After creating the new parameter, set the other required configuration:
    • Use: Private Key
    • Private Key: sftpKey
    • Username: exchange-user
    • Host: exchange-sftp-dev.10320.elluciancloud.com
  3. Run the test and the result should contain the list of files in the root folder, if a path is defined then it will show the contents of that instead.

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that has an array of file objects. File objects will contain the following properties:
  • filename - file name.
  • size - file size (in bytes).
  • modifyTime - file timestamp of last modified time.
  • accessTime - file timestamp of access time.
SFTP Get fitting

Use this fitting to perform a SFTP Get operation to download a file.

If your Integration pipeline uses SFTP fittings, your firewall rules, or the firewall rules of a third party, may need to allow for inbound requests. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected Input

Optional message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference Configuration

Configuration Description
Private Key Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the private key used for authentication. This or password must be present. Takes priority over password if defined.
Password Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the password used for authentication. This or privateKey must be present. Ignored if privateKey is defined.
Username Required. Can be interpolated, for example, {{message.payload.username}} or {{context.username}}.
Host Required.
File Name Required. Path to the remote file to download.
Port Optional. Default is 22. SFTP port supports Mustache expressions.

If the port is a number, use that number.

If the port is a Mustache expression, evaluate it. If it evaluated to a number, use that number instead of the default.

If the value is not a number or a Mustache expression, the value is not valid.
Binary Optional: Enables users to define the file transfer mode as binary instead of string.

Example

The following is an example of how to use SFTP Get.

  1. SFTP Get requires to define userName, host, fileName and either privateKeyor password. When using the private key it is necessary to create a parameter that will contain it, so make sure you have the following when creating SFTP parameter:
    • Create a parameter, for example,. "sftpKey" of type string, with Multi-line enabled.
    • The key should include the comments as well, for exmple, -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- ...etc
    • If getting file errors, make sure the path is correct, for example, . /home/fileName.txt or /fileName.txt instead of just fileName.txt.
  2. Because this example created a sftpKey parameter, the configuration will be using the privateKey. In the SFTP List example, the result contained a list of files from the root folder so, one of those is going to be used as the file name:
    • Use: Private Key
    • Private Key: sftpKey
    • Username: exchange-user
    • Host: exchange-sftp-dev.10320.elluciancloud.com
    • File Name: row2.txt
  3. After running the fitting, the response should show the content of that file.

Output

Content of the file in chunks.

Transformations

These fittings transform data.

Add to Context fitting

Use this fitting to add a data value from a message payload into the pipeline context, which is preserved from fitting to fitting.

Expected input

A message payload which is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Source Required. A JSON Path to a value in the payload
Target Required. The key to use when adding the value to context.

Output

The incoming message is pushed back into the pipeline.

Create Excel fitting

The Create Excel fitting converts an array of comma-separated value (CSV) strings into a Microsoft Excel (.xlsx) document.

Note: The Create Excel fitting is currently a beta release for customers testing new functionality.

It accepts CSV row data in the message payload and returns a binary Excel buffer for use in downstream fittings.

The Create Excel fitting supports the following:
  • Converting an array of CSV strings to Excel format
  • Parsing CSV correctly, including quoted fields and escaped characters
  • Binary Excel buffer output suitable for streaming or storage
  • Configurable input extraction using Source
  • Configurable error handling using Ignore Errors and Error Path
Common use cases include:
  • Generating downloadable Excel reports
  • Converting CSV output from upstream fittings into Excel format
  • Preparing structured exports for external systems
Best practices include:
  • Ensure the payload is a properly formatted, non-empty CSV string array
  • Validate upstream transformations before Excel generation
  • Set Target when the Excel output must be written, uploaded, or attached
  • For large datasets, consider chunking earlier in the pipeline

Expected input

The fitting expects an array of strings containing comma-separated values. By default, the fitting reads from the root of the message payload. If the CSV array is nested, use the Source field to specify a JSONPath to the input data.

Example input:

[
  "Name,Email,Department",
  "John Doe,john.doe@example.com,IT",
  "Jane Smith,jane.smith@example.com,HR",
  "Bob Johnson,bob.johnson@example.com,Finance"
]

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Source Optional. JSONPath to the CSV string array in the message payload. Leave blank to use the payload root.
Target Optional. Dot-notation path in the message to place the Excel buffer (for example, payload.report.excelFile).
Ignore Errors Optional. When set to true, disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use with Error Path to implement custom error handling. Default is false.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation path to store error information if processing fails. When set, the original message is forwarded with error details added at this path.

Example configuration:

{
  "name": "create-excel",
  "class": "CreateExcel",
  "config": {
    "source": "$.report.csvRows",
    "target": "payload.excelFile",
    "ignoreErrors": false,
    "errorPath": "payload.error"
  }
}

Output

The fitting generates a binary Excel (.xlsx) buffer. This buffer can be:

  • Written using File Writer
  • Passed to downstream fittings for further processing
Note: Set Target when the Excel buffer must be stored in the message payload for writing, uploading, or attaching.

Usage example - Basic usage (direct output)

{
  "name": "csv-to-excel",
  "class": "CreateExcel",
  "config": {}
}

Output: binary Excel buffer

Usage example - Target path

{
  "name": "csv-to-excel",
  "class": "CreateExcel",
  "config": {
    "target": "payload.report.excelFile"
  }
}

Output message structure:

{
  "header": {},
  "payload": {
    "report": {
      "excelFile": "<Excel Buffer>"
    }
  }
}

Usage example - Error handling

{
  "name": "csv-to-excel",
  "class": "CreateExcel",
  "config": {
    "target": "payload.excel",
    "errorPath": "payload.processingError"
  }

If an error occurs and Ignore Errors is On, the original message is pushed forward with error details added at the specified path.

CSV parsing features

The fitting includes CSV parsing support for:

  • Quoted fields (for example, "Smith, John","Developer","IT Department")
  • Escaped quotes (for example, "He said ""Hello""","Message")
  • Mixed content (for example, John,25,"Software Engineer","San Francisco, CA")

Error handling

The fitting provides:

  • Input validation (input must be a non-empty array)
  • CSV parsing error handling
  • Excel generation error handling
  • Optional error forwarding using Error Path

Performance considerations

The fitting builds the Excel file in memory before outputting. For very large datasets, consider chunking the data earlier in the pipeline. Excel files are compressed by default; memory usage scales with input size.

Example: Generate Excel file and upload to S3

The following is an example pipeline that transforms a message, generates an Excel file, and then writes it using an S3 sink.

[
  {
    "name": "transform",
    "class": "javascriptTransform",
    "config": {
      "code": "function transform (message, context) {\n  // Put your code here\n  const xlsxContent = [\n  \"First Name,Last Name,Email,Department,Job Title,Salary,Hire Date,Phone Number\",\n  \"John,Doe,john.doe@example.com,Engineering,Senior Engineer,120000,2018-03-15,555-0101\",\n  \"Jane,Smith,jane.smith@example.com,Human Resources,HR Manager,95000,2019-07-22,555-0102\",\n  ];\n  \n  message.payload = {\n    'report': {\n      'csvReport': xlsxContent\n    }\n  };\n  return message;\n}\n"
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "create-excel",
    "class": "CreateExcel",
    "config": {
      "source": "$.report.csvRows",
      "target": "payload.excelFile"
    }
  },
  {
    "name": "save-to-s3",
    "class": "S3Sink",
    "config": {
      "key": "reports/employee-report.xlsx",
      "bucket": "my-reports-bucket"
    }
  }
]
Create PDF fitting

The Create PDF fitting converts HTML or plain text into a professional, styled PDF document with full CSS support, pagination, and image rendering.

It accepts a complete HTML string or plain text in the message payload and returns a binary PDF buffer for use in downstream steps.

The Create PDF fitting supports the following:
  • High-fidelity HTML and CSS rendering
  • Inline and remote images
  • Pagination and custom page breaks
  • Binary PDF buffer output
Common use cases include:
  • Reports, invoices, certificates
  • System-generated summaries
  • Branded documents
Best practices include:
  • Use complete HTML (<html><head><body>)
  • Embed CSS in the <head> section
  • Use public URLs or base64 for images
  • Apply CSS for pagination control
  • Limit input to 5 MB; output must stay under 20 MB
  • Use JSONPath in the Source to extract HTML, if nested
  • Set the Error Path for troubleshooting; toggle Ignore Errors carefully

Expected input

The fitting expects the message payload to contain only the HTML string or plain text to be rendered as a PDF. Additional layout, pagination, and handling options can be configured separately in the input options section of the fitting.

Accepted input includes:
  • A valid, complete HTML document with a maximum input size of 5 MB
  • Plain text content with a maximum input size of 5 MB

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Orientation

Required. Select Portrait or Landscape.
Pagination Enables automatic page numbering. Default is Off.
Pagination Position Page Number: Add page numbers to the header or footer. Select In footer or In header. Default is In footer.
Source Optional. Leave this field blank for the payload root.
Target Optional. Dot-notation path to store the generated PDF buffer in the output message.
Ignore Errors Set to On to continue execution even if PDF rendering fails. Default is Off.
Error Path Path in the message payload to store rendering error details, if any.

Output

The target attribute is required to add the document as an attachment. The fitting generates a binary buffer representing the rendered PDF. This buffer can be:
  • Written to disk using File Writer
  • Uploaded through the SFTP Put fitting
  • Attached in the Send Notification fitting
Note: The target is required so it can be used as the attachment.

The PDF will retain all styling, layout, fonts, and embedded content as rendered from the HTML.

Maximum size of the final generated PDF is 20 MB.

When you use the Send Notification fitting to send the file as an attachment, the output must be under 5 MB.

Example: Zip PDF and write to Ellucian cloud storage

Create a pipeline to generate a PDF and save it as a ZIP file.

About this task

This pipeline formats HTML content, converts it into a PDF, and writes the resulting PDF into a ZIP file saved in Ellucian cloud storage.

Procedure

  1. In Ellucian Experience, click the Integration Designer card.
  2. Select or create a package:
    1. Select the Integration package where this new pipeline will be created.
    2. If needed, create a new package.
    3. In the Packages area, click +.
    4. Enter a unique name for the package.
    5. Optional: Add a description.
    6. Click Save.
    7. Select the new package from the list to continue.
  3. Create a new pipeline:
    1. In the Pipelines section, click + PIPELINE.
    2. Enter a unique name for the pipeline (for example, CreatePdf-ZIP).
    3. Optional: Add a description.
    4. Click Save.
    5. Click the pipeline name to open it.
  4. Configure the HTML Formatter fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select HTML Formatter.
    2. Enter HTML Formatter as the fitting name.
    3. Paste the following example into the Template field: 
      <!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8" />
  <title>Sample HTML Report</title>
  <style>
    body {
      font-family: Arial, sans-serif;
      padding: 2em;
      background: #f9f9f9;
    }
    h1 {
      color: #2c3e50;
    }
    p {
      line-height: 1.6;
    }
    .section {
      margin-top: 20px;
      padding: 10px;
      background: #ffffff;
      border-radius: 5px;
      box-shadow: 0 0 4px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1);
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <h1>Monthly Performance Report</h1>
  <div class="section">
    <h2>Overview</h2>
    <p>This report provides a summary of activity for the month of May.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="section">
    <h2>Key Metrics</h2>
    <p>Revenue: $45,000<br>New Users: 1,200<br>Retention Rate: 87%</p>
  </div>
</body>
</html>
    4. Click Save.
  5. Configure the Create PDF fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select Create PDF.
    2. Enter Create PDF as the fitting name.
    3. Set Orientation to Portrait.
    4. Set Pagination to On.
    5. Set Pagination Position to In footer.
    6. Leave Ignore Errors set to Off.
    7. Click Save.
  6. Configure the File Writer fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select File Writer.
    2. Enter File Writer as the fitting name.
    3. Set Key to testfile.pdf.
    4. Set Include total count to On.
    5. Set Generate Presigned URL to On.
    6. Set Write Immediately to Off.
    7. Click Save.
  7. Configure the JavaScript Transform fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select JavaScript Transform.
    2. Enter JavaScript Transform as the fitting name.
    3. Set Push Undefined to On.
    4. Paste the following code snippet into the editor: 
      function transform (message, context) {
  message.payload.testfile = ['testfile.pdf'];
  return message;
}
    5. Click Save.
  8. Configure the Create Zip File fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select Create Zip File.
    2. Enter Create Zip File as the fitting name.
    3. Set File Name Path to $.testfile.
    4. Set Output File Name to output.zip.
    5. Click Save.

Results

This pipeline formats an HTML page, generates a styled PDF and compresses it into a ZIP file named output.zip. The PDF is stored in Ellucian cloud storage.
