    7. Click Test.
  5. To iterate student workers, configure the For Each fitting.
    1. From the Transformations menu, click For Each.
    2. Enter Iterate Student Workers as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Iterates over each student worker record in the mock data collection.
    4. Enter payload.studentWorkers in the Source field.
    5. Click Test.
  6. To specify the path to where to extract the data from before you convert the data into a CSV file, configure the Delimited Formatter fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select Delimited Formatter.
    2. Enter Format Data as CSV as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Formats the mock student worker data into a CSV structure with selected columns including name, salary grade, annual salary, position code, and title.
    4. Set Normalize Columns to False.
    5. Turn Column Headers True.
      Column paths from the Extract Data transform display in the Columns field.
    6. Click Test.
      The data is now formatted to write to a CSV file.
  7. To write that formatted data to the CSV file, configure the File Writer fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select File Writer.
    2. Enter Write CSV to Temporary Storage as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Writes the formatted CSV data to temporary S3 storage for subsequent encryption processing.
    4. Enter a File Name. For example, studentWorkers.csv.
    5. Set Add New Line After Each Message to True.
    6. Set Include Total Count to False.
    7. Set Generate Presigned Url to True.
    8. Set Write Immediately to False.
    9. Set UTF Encoding to UTF-8.
    10. Click Test.
  8. Configure the File Reader fitting:
    1. From the Sources menu, select File Reader.
    2. Enter Read CSV File as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Reads the CSV file from S3 temporary storage to prepare it for encryption.
    4. Set Key to {{context.__pipelineName}}/{{context.__runId}}/studentWorkers.csv.
    5. Set Binary to False.
    6. Set Allow Concurrent to False.
    7. Click Test.
  9. Configure the Encrypt Data fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select Encrypt Data.
    2. Enter Encrypt Data with PGP as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Encrypts the CSV file content using PGP encryption with the provided public key and signs it with the private key for authenticity.
    4. Select the Public Key parameter publicKeyEncrypt that you set up in the pipeline parameters earlier from the drop-down list.
    5. Set Signature to True.
      The Private Key becomes required.
    6. Enter privateKeyEncrypt for the Private Key and passphraseEncrypt for the Passphrase.
    7. Leave the Binary setting as the default setting True to return encrypted data in binary format.
    8. Set Ignore Errors to False.
    9. Click Test.
  10. Configure the SFTP Put fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select SFTP Put.
    2. Enter Upload Encrypted File to SFTP as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Securely uploads the encrypted GPG file to the configured SFTP server using private key authentication.
    4. Enter privateKeySFTP for the Private Key.
    5. Enter {{context.sftpUsername}} for the User Name.
    6. Enter {{context.sftpHost}} for the Host.
    7. Enter {{context.sftpFilePath}} for the File Path.
    8. Set Push to True.
    9. Click Test.

Results

The pipeline generates a PGP-encrypted .gpg file containing the student worker data in CSV format. The file is uploaded to the specified SFTP location with the configured filename.
Example: Extract a list and encrypt and upload to SFTP

Create a pipeline that extracts student worker records from Banner, formats the data as CSV, encrypts it using the Encrypt Data fitting with PGP, and uploads the encrypted file to an SFTP server.

About this task

This is the production pipeline that performs the following steps:
  • Extract Data: Queries Banner for active student worker records including employee details, position information, and salary data.
  • Delimited Formatter: Formats the extracted data into a CSV structure with selected columns.
  • File Writer: Stores the formatted CSV in S3 temporary storage.
  • File Reader: Reads the CSV file from temporary storage for encryption.
  • Encrypt Data: Encrypts the file using PGP encryption and signs it with a digital signature.
  • SFTP Put: Securely uploads the encrypted GPG file to the configured SFTP server.

Procedure

  1. In Ellucian Experience, click the Integration Designer card.
  2. Select or create a package:
    1. Select the Integration package where this new pipeline will be created.
    2. If needed, create a new package.
    3. In the Packages area, click +.
    4. Enter a unique name for the package.
    5. Optional: Add a description.
    6. Click Save.
    7. Select the new package from the list to continue.
  3. Create a new pipeline:
    1. In the Pipelines area, click + PIPELINE.
    2. Enter a unique name for the pipeline. For example, Encrypt Student Worker Data Pipeline.
    3. Optional: Add a description. For example, This pipeline extracts student worker data from Banner, formats it as a CSV file, encrypts it using PGP encryption, and securely transfers the encrypted file to an SFTP server.
    4. Click Save.
    5. Click the pipeline name to open it.
    6. To set up parameters, near the pipeline name, click the drop-down menu and select Edit Pipeline Settings.
    7. Add the following new pipeline parameters:
      1. publicKeyEncrypt
        • Label: PGP Public Key
        • Description: The PGP public key used to encrypt the student worker data file.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
        • Sensitive: True
        • Multiline: True
        • Persistent: True
      2. privateKeyEncrypt
        • Label: PGP Private Key for Signing
        • Description: The PGP private key used to sign the encrypted file for authenticity verification.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
        • Sensitive: True
        • Multiline: True
        • Persistent: True
      3. passphraseEncrypt
        • Label: PGP Passphrase
        • Description: The passphrase associated with the PGP private key used for signing.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
        • Sensitive: True
        • Persistent: True
      4. privateKeySFTP
        • Label: SFTP Private Key
        • Description: The private key used for authenticating with the SFTP server.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
        • Sensitive: True
        • Multiline: True
        • Persistent: True
      5. sftpUsername
        • Label: SFTP Username
        • Description: The username for authenticating with the SFTP server.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
      6. sftpHost
        • Label: SFTP Host
        • Description: The hostname or IP address of the SFTP server.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
      7. sftpFilePath
        • Label: SFTP Destination File Path
        • Description: The full file path on the SFTP server where the encrypted file will be uploaded.
        • Type: String
        • Required: True
    8. Click Save.
  4. To build the first segment for this example, configure the Extract Data fitting:
    1. from the Insights Transformations menu, click Extract Data.
    2. Enter Extract Data - Extract Student Worker Data from Banner as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Extracts active student worker records from Banner, including employee details, position information, and salary data.
    4. Enter the SQL inquiry that will collect the active student worker data from the Banner database.
      This pulls the active student worker data, For example, name, salary, position, employment status. For this example, enter the following SQL statement.
      SELECT spriden_id,
       NBRJOBS_ORGN_CODE_TS,
       PEBEMPL_ORGN_CODE_HOME,
       PEBEMPL_ORGN_CODE_DIST,
       nbrjobs_posn,
       NBBPOSN_GRADE,
       NBBPOSN_TITLE,
       NBBPOSN_EXEMPT_IND,
       NBBPOSN_POSN_REPORTS,
       NBRJOBS_SAL_GRADE,
       nbrjobs_ann_salary,
       spriden_last_name,
       spriden_first_name,
       nbrjobs_suff,
       nbrjobs_ecls_code
FROM nbrjobs a,
     NBBPOSN,
     spbpers,
     pebempl,
     spriden
WHERE nbrjobs_pidm = spriden_pidm
  AND spriden_pidm = pebempl_pidm
  AND spriden_pidm = spbpers_pidm
  AND nbrjobs_posn = nbbposn_posn
  AND spriden_change_ind IS NULL
  AND a.nbrjobs_status <> 'T'
  AND a.nbrjobs_ecls_code IN ('US', 'ST', 'GB', 'NR')
  AND nbrjobs_effective_date = (
        SELECT MAX(nbrjobs_effective_date)
        FROM nbrjobs b
        WHERE nbrjobs_effective_date <= now()
          AND b.nbrjobs_pidm = a.nbrjobs_pidm
          AND b.nbrjobs_posn = a.nbrjobs_posn
          AND b.nbrjobs_suff = a.nbrjobs_suff
      )
ORDER BY spriden_last_name,
         spriden_first_name,
         a.nbrjobs_posn;
    5. Set Bulk Load Enabled to True.
    6. Set Ignore Errors to False.
    7. Click Save.
  5. To specify the path to where to extract the data from before you convert the data into a CSV file, configure the Delimited Formatter fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select Delimited Formatter.
    2. Enter Delimited Formatter - Format Data as CSV as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Formats the extracted student worker data into a CSV structure with selected columns including name, salary grade, annual salary, position code, and title.
    4. Set Normalize Columns to False.
    5. Turn Column Headers to True.
      Column paths from the Extract Data transform display in the Columns field.
      [
            {
              "path": "spriden_first_name"
            },
            {
              "path": "spriden_last_name"
            },
            {
              "path": "nbrjobs_sal_grade"
            },
            {
              "path": "nbrjobs_ann_salary"
            },
            {
              "path": "nbrjobs_posn"
            },
            {
              "path": "nbbposn_title"
            }
          ]
    6. Click Save.
      The data is now formatted to write to a CSV file.
  6. To write that formatted data to the CSV file, configure the File Writer fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select File Writer.
    2. Enter File Writer - Write formatted student worker data to a csv file as the fitting name.
    3. Enter a File Name. For example, studentWorkers.csv.
    4. Set Add New Line After Each Message to True.
    5. Set Include Total Count to False.
    6. Set Generate Presigned Url to True.
    7. Set Write Immediately to False.
    8. Set UTF Encoding to UTF-8.
    9. Click Save.
  7. Configure the File Reader fitting:
    1. From the Sources menu, select File Reader.
    2. Enter File Reader - Read the file from S3 as the fitting name.
    3. Set Key to {{context._pipelineName}}/{{context._runId}}/studentWorkers.csv.
    4. Click Save.
      The File Reader reads the message and places it into a single payload, as the Encrypt Data fitting requires a single payload. It is recommended when there are multiple messages that you use a Reducer fitting to place the message into a single payload.
  8. Configure the Encrypt Data fitting:
    1. From the Transformations menu, select Encrypt Data.
    2. Enter Encrypt Data - Encrypt retrieved data as the fitting name.
    3. Select the Public Key parameter publicKeyEncrypt that you set up in the pipeline parameters earlier from the drop-down list.
    4. If Signature is set to True, the Private Key becomes required.
    5. Optional: Enter privateKeyEncrypt for the Private Key and passphraseEncrypt for the Passphrase.
    6. Leave the Binary setting as the default setting True to return encrypted data in binary format.
    7. Click Save.
  9. Configure the SFTP Put fitting:
    1. From the Destinations menu, select SFTP Put.
    2. Enter SFTP Put - Upload Encrypted File to SFTP as the fitting name.
    3. Optional: Enter a description. For example, Securely uploads the encrypted GPG file to the configured SFTP server using private key authentication.
    4. Enter privateKeySFTP for the Private Key.
    5. Enter {{context.sftpUsername}} for the User Name.
    6. Enter {{context.sftpHost}} for the Host.
    7. Enter {{context.sftpFilePath}} for the File Path.
    8. Set Push to True.
    9. Click Save.

Results

The pipeline generates a PGP-encrypted .gpg file containing the student worker data in CSV format. The file is uploaded to the specified SFTP location with the configured filename.
Ethos Consume Confirm fitting

The Ethos Consume Confirm fitting marks an event (change notification or business event) as processed. The provided last processed ID is persisted by this fitting, and is used at the starting point by the Ethos Consume Event fitting when the pipeline executes next.

Confirming event ID N advances the subscriber's last processed ID and implicitly confirms all prior events because events are delivered in order. The Confirm fitting must be reached to ensure forward progress of the subscriber queue.

Expected input

This fitting requires the ID of the last event that was successfully processed. It can be contained in context or in the message (this is more typical).

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Last Processed Id Required. ID of the last event that was successfully processed. This can be lastProcessedId of the message payload or lastProcessedId from context.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: error is the same as payload.error.
API Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter that will contain an alternate API key this fitting will use for Ethos requests. When the parameter is not specified ethosApiKey will be used by default.

Expected configuration

{
  "class": "ethosConfirmConsume",
  "config": {
    "lastProcessedId": "{{msg.header.lastProcessedId}}", // Required - id of the last event that was successfully processed. This can be "{{msg.payload.lastProcessedId}}" or "{{context.lastProcessedId}}"
    "apiKey": "string", // Optional - Name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified `ethosApiKey` will be used.
    "errorPath": "string", // Optional - Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error"
    "ignoreErrors": "boolean" // Optional flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
  }
}

Example fitting configuration

"consumeConfirm": {
  "class": "ethosConsumeConfirm",
  "config": {
    "lastProcessedId": "{{msg.header.lastProcessedId}}",
    "errorPath": "error"
  }
}

Output

None

Ethos Proxy Delete fitting

Use this fitting to perform a delete operation on an Ethos resource through Ethos Integration.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example persons.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

When selecting the DELETE method in the API Selector, if there are multiple DELETE methods displayed, select the method with the path that does not include {id}.

After you select the resource, the resource you selected and the version you selected are populated on the Ethos Proxy Delete fitting page.

If you select a major or minor version, the major version is automatically populated, so that the user is pinned to the floating major version. If the user selects a patch version, the specific patch version is populated in Data Connect.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Content Version

Required if Body Path is set. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.
Accept Version

Required if Body Path is set. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.
Alternative Content Representation Optional. Alternative content representation.
Body Path Optional. A JSON Path in the payload which will be used as the body of the request. If set but the path returns undefined, no operation will be done and the message will be pushed through.
Get Id from Payload Optional. JSONPath to id within payload itself. Mutually exclusive from Id from Context. For example, $.person.id.
Get Id from Context Optional. JSONPath to id within context. Mutually exclusive from Id from Payload. For example, $.guid.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: error is the same as payload.error.
API Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter, which will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that is the response. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

If neither idFromPayload, idFromContext, nor bodyPath are specified, no HTTP request is made. The original input message is passed through to the next fitting unchanged.

When idFromPayload or idFromContext is configured with an invalid JSONPath expression that causes an evaluation error, the Ethos resource is not reached, an error is reported to the Ethos errors API, and the original input message is passed through to the next fitting. If the JSONPath is syntactically valid but resolves to no value, the message is similarly passed through but no error is reported.

Ethos Proxy Delete fitting example - by resource ID

For this fitting to work, start by creating an Ethos API Key as a parameter.

Procedure

  1. Near the pipeline name, click the drop-down menu and select Edit Pipeline Settings.
  2. Add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the configuration.
  3. Configure the fitting. For example:
    Field Example selection or entry
    Resource persons
    Get Id From Payload
    Id From Payload $.student.id
Ethos Proxy Delete fitting example - by request body

For this fitting to work, start by creating an Ethos API Key as a parameter.

Procedure

  1. Near the pipeline name, click the drop-down menu and select Edit Pipeline Settings.
  2. Add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the configuration.
  3. Configure the fitting. For example:
    Field Example selection or entry
    Resource emergency-contacts
    Content Version 1.0.0
    Accept Version 1.0.0
    Body Path $.deleteRequestBody

    This value is assumed to be set in the message payload by a preceding fitting in the pipeline.
    Get Id From None
File Attributes fitting

Use the file attributes fitting to retrieve the metadata for an object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Key Required. S3 object key. Value supports interpolation.
Target Optional. Payload target. Supports dot-notation structure.

Key interpolation

The Key field and the message payload's s3.object.key both accept interpolation tags that will take into account values in context and processed message, including header and payload.

Some examples of key values:

  • sample-file.txt - Simple hardcoded value (no interpolation)
  • {{context.filename}} - Interpolated value from context
  • {{message.header.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.header
  • {{message.payload.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.payload
  • sample-folder/{{context.filename}} - Combination of hardcoded folder with interpolated file name from context
  • {{context.foldername}}/{{message.payload.filename}} - Combination of two interpolated values from both context and message.payload

Example

The following is an example of how to use File Attributes fitting

  1. The file attributes fitting only needs the key of a file that exists in S3. In the File List example, a list of files with the prefix person is retrieved. One of those is named persons-id-10.txt and contains a list of ten person IDs. Use persons-ids-10.txt as Key.

  2. After running the example, the metadata information of the file will be retrieved in the payload.

Output

The metadata of the file in JSON format.

File Delete fitting

Use the file delete fitting to delete a file from S3.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Key Required. S3 object key. Value supports interpolation.
Bucket Optional. The name of the parameter (context entry) containing an S3 bucket name.
Access Key Id Required if using the bucket option. The name of the parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Access Key ID.
Secret Access Key Required if using the bucket option. The name of the parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Access key.

Key interpolation

The key field and the message payload's s3.object.key both accept interpolation tags that will take into account values in context and processed message, including header and payload.

Some examples of key values:

  • sample-file.txt - Simple hardcoded value (no interpolation)
  • {{context.filename}} - Interpolated value from context
  • {{message.header.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.header
  • {{message.payload.filename}} - Interpolated value from message.payload
  • sample-folder/{{context.filename}} - Combination of hardcoded folder with interpolated filename from context
  • {{context.foldername}}/{{message.payload.filename}} - Combination of two interpolated values from both context and message.payload

Output

None

Fixed Width Formatter fitting

Use this fitting to format a data stream into a fixed-width report.

Expected input

The formatter expects each stream message payload to be an object. Payloads that are not of type object will be ignored by the fitting with no pass-through.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form, Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition, are common to all fittings.

Configuration Description
End of Line Optional. The end of line (EOL) configuration provides a way to specify a line delimiter. By default no EOL character is appended to each row, it is up to the following segments in a pipeline to make sure each line is delimited.
Header Optional. Headers may be used to enhance a report's structure and data understanding.
Detail Required At least one detail column is required The 'detail' configuration defines how each message payload is handled and laid out on each detail row.
Footer Optional. Footer rows are optional content rows that can aid in the final report presentation or format. The footer row is the last one to be displayed. For example, a footer row can contain totals.

Header

Configuration Description
Include on Empty Detail Optional. Flag to force a header or footer row when no detail rows were processed.
Width Required if header is added. Column value maximum width. Because this is a fixed width based fitting, if the width exceeds the actual value length padding will happen (with spaces by default.) On the other hand, if the value length exceeds the specified width, value will be truncated to fit.
Type Optional. When the source is specified as a simple string it is used as a path to map the column's value from the payload message object. More control is gained when the object definition is used. Source type definition path will use the configured value as a mapping path. Literal means the value will be used as entered. Lastly, eval values will be evaluated as JavaScript expressions.
Value Required if header is added. Depending on the specified type the value will have different connotations. Interpolation is allowed within this property regardless of the type, it also has precedence meaning it happens before mapping, evaluation, or simple use of it.
Transformation Functions Optional. Series of transformation functions applied to the queried source value. When more than one function is specified the series is executed in the order in which they are listed. The source value will always be automatically sent as a parameter to the functions.
Name Optional. Column name. This value has two purposes: documentation and redaction reference.
Description Optional column description. This value has no functional consequences, it is for documentation purposes only.
Align Optional. Column value alignment. Possible values: left, right, and center. If there is enough spare space within a column's value, padding will happen towards the end when aligned to left, and towards the start when aligned right. Finally, when aligned to center an equal distribution of the padding character will happen at the start and end of the column. By default values are aligned left.
Pad Optional. Column padding character combination. When more than one character is specified, the word will be repeated X amount of times until column width is satisfied. Padding will never cause column overflow. By default padding character is a space character.
Overflow Optional. Character combination to identify value truncation. If a value is truncated, the overflow sequence will be added at the end of the column's value. If the overflow's own length exceeds the available length to display the truncated value it will be ignored. Overflow is always displayed at the end of the column value, no matter the alignment. By default no overflow character is used.

Detail

Configuration Description
Columns Required. List of columns that will make up the detail row composition.
Width Required. Column value maximum width. Because this is a fixed-width based fitting, if the width exceeds the actual value length padding will happen, with spaces by default. On the other hand, if the value length exceeds the specified width, the value will be truncated to fit.
Type Optional. When the source is specified as a simple string it is used as a path to map the column's value from the payload message object. More control is gained when the object definition is used. Source type definition path will use the configured value as a mapping path. Literal means the value will be used as entered. Lastly, eval values will be evaluated as JavaScript expressions.
Value Required. Depending on the specified type the value will have different connotations. Interpolation is allowed within this property regardless of the type, it also has precedence meaning it happens before mapping, evaluation, or simple use of it.
Transformation Functions Optional. Series of transformation functions applied to the queried source value. When more than one function is specified the series is executed in the order in which they are listed. The source value will always be automatically sent as a parameter to the functions.
Name Optional. Column name. This value has two purposes: documentation and redaction reference.
Description Optional column description. This value has no functional consequences, it is for documentation purposes only.
Align Optional. Column value alignment. Possible values: left, right, and center. If there is enough spare space within a column's value, padding will happen towards the end when aligned to left, and towards the start when aligned right. Finally, when aligned to center an equal distribution of the padding character will happen at the start and end of the column. By default values are aligned left.
Pad Optional. Column padding character combination. When more than one character is specified, the word will be repeated X amount of times until column width is satisfied. Padding will never cause column overflow. By default padding character is a space character.
Overflow Optional. Character combination to identify value truncation. If a value is truncated, the overflow sequence will be added at the end of the column's value. If the overflow's own length exceeds the available length to display the truncated value it will be ignored. Overflow is always displayed at the end of the column value no matter the alignment. By default no overflow character is used.
Accumulators Accumulators are defined buckets to analyze incoming data. These accumulators can be used by means of interpolation. Interpolation can be achieved by using mustache type placeholders, which are replaced at runtime Example.'{{context.runId}}' : Returns the pipeline's runId within the pipeline context. Additional details on Accumulators are available below.
Redaction Rules Optional. Redaction rules. When specified the defined columns will be redacted from the resulting row data with a mask. Both redact fields, columns and mask, can be interpolated.
Columns Optional. List of column names to be redacted. It is very important that if redaction is going to be used, all detail columns must have defined names, otherwise, redaction will be ignored.
Mask Optional masking character or word. When a single character is specified, its value will be used to replace each character of the matching column's value. If a word is specified as a mask, the word will be used (once) as the column's value instead. Masked values will still respect the column's width rules. By default, a space character is used.
`

Footer

Configuration Description
Include on Empty Detail Optional. Flag to force a header or footer row when no detail rows were processed.
Width Required if footer is added. Column value maximum width. Because this is a fixed width based fitting, if the width exceeds the actual value length padding will happen (with spaces by default.) On the other hand, if the value length exceeds the specified width, value will be truncated to fit.
Type Optional. When the source is specified as a simple string it is used as a path to map the column's value from the payload message object. More control is gained when the object definition is used. Source type definition path will use the configured value as a mapping path. Literal means the value will be used as entered. Lastly, eval values will be evaluated as JavaScript expressions.
Value Required if footer is added. Depending on the specified type the value will have different connotations. Interpolation is allowed within this property regardless of the type, it also has precedence, meaning it happens before mapping, evaluation, or simple use of it.
Transformation Functions Optional. Series of transformation functions applied to the queried source value. When more than one function is specified the series is executed in the order in which they are listed. The source value will always be automatically sent as a parameter to the functions.
Name Optional. Column name. This value has two purposes: documentation and redaction reference.
Description Optional column description. This value has no functional consequences, it is for documentation purposes only.
Align Optional. Column value alignment. Possible values: left, right, and center. If there is enough spare space within a column's value, padding will happen towards the end when aligned to left, and towards the start when aligned right. Finally, when aligned to center an equal distribution of the padding character will happen at the start and end of the column. By default values are aligned left.
Pad Optional. Column padding character combination. When more than one character is specified, the word will be repeated X amount of times until column width is satisfied. Padding will never cause column overflow. By default padding character is a space character.
Overflow Optional. Character combination to identify value truncation. If a value is truncated, the overflow sequence will be added at the end of the column's value. If the overflow's own length exceeds the available length to display the truncated value it will be ignored. Overflow is always displayed at the end of the column value, no matter the alignment. By default no overflow character is used.

Examples

The only required configuration field is detail.columns. The rest of the optional fields are either ignored or defaulted.

  • Column01:

    • Width: 3

    • Type: Path

    • Value: column1

  • Column02:

    • Width: 10

    • Type: Path

    • Value: column2

  • Column03:

    • Width: 3

    • Type: Path

    • Value: column3

{
  "class": "fixedWidthFormatter",
  "config": {
    "detail": {
      "columns": [
        { "source": "column1", "width": 3 },
        { "source": "column2", "width": 10 },
        { "source": "column3", "width": 3 }
      ]
    }
  }
}

A series of payloads:

// Payload 1
{ column1: 'foo1', column2: 'bar1', column3: 'baz1' }
// Payload 2
{ column1: 'foo2', column2: 'bar2', column3: 'baz2' }
// Payload 3
{ column1: 'foo3', column2: 'bar3', column3: 'baz3' }

Will be formatted as:

foobar1      baz
foobar2      baz
foobar3      baz

Based on the configured mapping:

  • Each payload object field with key column1, column2, and column3 will be formatted into a fixed width row

  • column1 and column3 values have been truncated to their widths (3 characters)

  • column2 values have been padded with spaces to fill the expected columns width (10 characters)

Interpolation

Interpolation can be achieved by using mustache type placeholders, which are replaced at runtime.

For fields that support it, interpolation interpretation will always happen before logic makes use of its value. When the referenced data is not of a primitive type, such as an object or array, the interpolation logic will try its best to return the data with its expected type. This is useful when mapping values are to be sent to transformation logic, or to be evaluated with JavaScript logic.

Interpolation in the FixedWidthFormatter can reference data from the following sources: (incoming) Message, Context, and Accumulators. When an interpolation reference is specified but cannot be mapped to an existing value, it is replaced with empty string.

Examples:

  • {{context.runId}} : Returns the pipeline's runId within the pipeline context.

  • {{message.payload.data}} : Returns the data field within the processed message's payload.

  • {{accumulators.total}} : Returns the value in the defined detail accumulator.

Fixed Width Parser fitting

Use this fitting to parse content from a fixed-width string into objects based on column definitions.

Expected input

The parser expects each stream message payload to be of type string. Non-string payloads will be ignored by the fitting with no pass-through.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form, Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition, are common to all fittings.

Configuration Description
Skip Lines Optional. Number of lines to be ignored from the beginning of a transmission. If skipLines is set to 5 when processing a 10 line fixed width file, the first 5 lines will be ignored, processing will happen only on last 5 lines. This is useful when a file contains a header section that needs no processing. By default no lines are skipped.
Include Row Type Optional. Setting to include the type of row (header, detail, or footer) that was processed as part of the payload. When includeRowType is true, the payload field will be of the type that was selected. A different field name can be specified if a string value is set instead of boolean. Dot notation is also allowed when setting a new type field name. By default no row type is included in any of the message payloads.
Header Optional header setup. If Header is included, either column or definition must be present.
Detail Required detail setup.
Footer Optional footer setup.

Section configuration

A section can be defined as a flat or as a nested record definition by configuring plain columns or definitions.

Configuration Description
End Of Data Optional. Regular expression object to identify a data row that marks the end of data for a section. Must contain a valid regular expression string.
Flags Optional. Flags to be applied to the expression.
Rows Optional. Number to specify how many rows need to be processed in a given section. When rows is specified and reached, the section will not process more data. For example, a header with two rows will always process only two messages before transferring data to the details section. By default there is no row limit to a section.
Column Required if header is added and definition is not included. Provides a way to specify a fixed column setup that will be used for all data rows processed by the section. When columns are specified, definitions cannot be set.
Definitions Required if header is added and column is not included. Provides a way to setup specialized parsing for different kinds of data rows. Definitions is an object that can contain one or more named definition. The definition's property name itself will be used to match the first data row characters if no match criteria was set. Specifying definitions is a great way to handle data row collections that can have different structures. When definitions are specified, columns at the section level cannot be set.

Definitions

Definitions provide a way to set up specialized parsing for different kinds of data rows. Definitions is an object that can contain one or more named definition. The definition's property name itself will be used to match the first data row characters if no match criteria was set. Specifying definitions is a great way to handle data row collections that can have different structures. When definitions are specified, columns at the section level cannot be set.

Configuration Description
Definition Name Required if definition is added. Name of the definition.
Match Optional. Data row matching criteria. When not specified, the definition's property name will be used to match.
Ignore the Definition Optional. Flag to ignore the definition. All data rows matching a definition with ignore set to true will be skipped.
Name Optional. Name to be used to identify the definition within the record structure. When no name is specified the property name will be used.
Description Optional. Definition description. This has no functional purpose, only documentation.
Is Loop Optional. Flag to define the definition as a loop. A loop means that sequential repetitions of the definition will be treated as a list.
Other definitions that can be contained Optional. List of other definitions that can be contained within. Only definition property names will be considered.
Columns Optional. List of columns. The whole list will define how data will be parsed within the definition. Columns are always required unless the ignore flag was set to true.

Example definition configuration:

  • Definition01:

    • Definition Name: AA

    • Enter other definitions that can be contained: BB - CC (Click the + button after entering each parameter.)

    • Columns -> Name: greeting

    • Columns -> Width: 14

    • Columns -> Type: String

    • Columns -> Align: Left

  • Definition02:

    • Definition Name: BB

    • Name: innerBB

    • Is Loop: ON

    • Columns -> Name: message

    • Columns -> Width: 14

    • Columns -> Type: String

    • Columns -> Align: Left

  • Definition03:

    • Definition Name: CC

    • Is Loop: ON

    • Columns -> Name: message

    • Columns -> Width: 14

    • Columns -> Type: String

    • Columns -> Align: Left

{
  "class": "fixedWidthParser",
  "config": {
    "detail": {
      "definitions": {
        "AA": { // AA is the definition name
          "canContain": [ "BB", "CC" ],
          "columns": [
            { "name": "greeting", "width": 14 }
          ]
        },
        "BB": {
          "name": "innerBB",
          "isLoop": true,
          "columns": [
            { "name": "message", "width": 14 }
          ]
        },
        "CC": {
          "isLoop": true,
          "columns": [
            { "name": "message", "width": 14 }
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  }
}

Will parse the following data messages:

AAHello
BBInner B Data 1
BBInner B Data 2
CCInner C Data 1
CCInner C Data 2

As a single message payload with the following structure:

{
  greeting: 'Hello',
  innerBB: [
    { message: 'Inner B Data 1' },
    { message: 'Inner B Data 2' }
  ],
  CC: [
    { message: 'Inner C Data 1' },
    { message: 'Inner C Data 2' }
  ]
}

Columns

A column is the most basic piece of configuration of a fixed-width record. It will define how a bit of information is interpreted and organized within the resulting structure.

Configuration Description
Name Required. Column name. It serves two purposes, documentation and to name the property in which the information will be stored. It supports dot-notation, allowing for simple and complex data structures.
Width Required. Width defines the length in characters.
Ignore the column Optional. Flag to ignore the column. This is convenient to handle and ignore filler columns.
Start Position Optional. Data starting position. It forces the parameter to be read from a specific position. Normally data is read in a sequential fashion, starting at 0 index and moving forward using the previous field width to move to the next one. Be aware that by using startPosition, the sequence is forced back or forward, potentially missing or repeating data.
Description Optional. Definition description. This has no functional purpose, only documentation.
Type Optional. Type definition. Options are String, number, Boolean and date. If not specified string is used as the default type. If number, Boolean, or date is chosen additional values can be configured.
Pad Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Pad character specification. When present, any matching leading or trailing characters, depending on alignment, will be removed. By default the space character is used to match padding. Displayed if number is chosen as type.
Number Implicit Decimals Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Numeric parameters that specifies how many decimal spaces a number must contain when implicit decimal point format is used. This is very common on legacy systems where space was of the essence. For example, the number 314 with 2 implicit decimal positions means that the number must be interpreted as 3.14.
Number Symbol Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Number symbol to be ignored when parsing a numeric field that would otherwise make the conversion to number not successful. For example, dollar signs ($), percent (%), or the pound sign (#).
Number Is Accounting Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Flag to identify a numeric field as an accounting type. This specifically deals with negative numbers enclosed in parenthesis rather than using the minus (-) sign.
Number Base Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Number base (or radix). Possible values: 2, 8, 10, and 16 for binary, octal, decimal, and hexadecimal respectively. By default all numbers are expected to be base 10 (decimal). When a base other than 10 is used, all other number format properties are ignored except numberSymbol.
Pad Optional. Displayed when type Boolean is selected. Pad character specification. When present, any matching leading or trailing characters, depending on alignment, will be removed. By default the space character is used to match padding. Displayed if number is chosen as type.
Boolean True Optional. Displayed when type Boolean is selected. True value match. When specified, if the mapped value matches the booleanTrue string, the field value will be set to true.
Boolean False Optional. Displayed when type Boolean is selected. False value match. When specified, if the mapped value matches the booleanFalse string, the field value will be set to false.
Boolean Allow Unset Optional. Displayed when type Boolean is selected. Flag that when true it will allow a boolean field to be undefined in the resulting field value. This flag works in tandem with the booleanTrue and booleanFalse properties.
Pad Optional. Displayed when type date is selected. Pad character specification. When present, any matching leading or trailing characters, depending on alignment, will be removed. By default the space character is used to match padding. Displayed if date is chosen as type.
Date Format Optional. Displayed when type date is selected. Date format or formats. It allows for a single string or list of possible formats to be expected.
Date ISO 8601 Optional. Displayed when type date is selected. Flag that enables date parsing using ISO 8601 compatible formats.
Align Optional. Value alignment. By default left alignment is assumed.
Pad Optional. Pad character specification. When present, any matching leading or trailing characters, depending on alignment, will be removed. By default the space character is used to match padding.

Example

The only required configuration field is either detail.columns or detail.definitions.

  • Rows: 0

  • column01:

    • Name: column1

    • Width: 10

    • Type: String

    • Align: Left

  • column02:

    • Name: column2

    • Width: 5

    • Type: Number

    • Align: Left

    • Number Base: Decimal

{
  "class": "fixedWidthParser",
  "config": {
    "detail": {
      "columns": [
        { "name": "column1", "width": 10 },
        { "name": "column2", "width": 5, "type": "number" }
      ]
    }
  }
}

A series of string payloads from file:

Foo       12345
Bar       98765
Baz       00000

Will be parsed as object payloads:

// Payload 1
{ column1: 'Foo', column2: 12345 }
// Payload 2
{ column1: 'Bar', column2: 98765 }
// Payload 3
{ column1: 'Baz', column2: 0 }
For Each fitting

Use the For Each fitting to iterate over an incoming array and push a new message for each item.

For Each fitting splits off separate threads for each item and runs them in parallel. It does not act on them sequentially.

Expected input

A message payload or payload property that is a JavaScript array.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Source Optional. Specify the payload property to iterate.

Output

For each item in the incoming array, a new message with the same header as the incoming message and a payload with the item.

HTML Formatter fitting

Use the HTML Formatter fitting to produce HTML output based on a template where you can combine HTML content and Mustache tag placeholders.

The fitting allows parsing the Mustache tags and replacing them with values to produce dynamic output based on data provided. Integration Designer uses mustache.js for processing any mustache tags that are included.

For more information on Mustache tag expressions, see https://mustache.github.io/mustache.5.html.

Expected input

The fitting accepts, but does not require, a single message payload. Use a Reducer fitting, if needed, to consolidate multiple messages sent by a prior fitting. If data from the payload is to be referenced by the Mustache tag placeholders, then payload has to be in the form of one or more JSON objects.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Template Required. HTML content with or without Mustache expressions. If payload data is referenced from the Mustache tags, ensure the tags reference the full structure, such as {{message.payload.field}} or the corresponding property where the JSON data objects are stored.

Output

After processing any Mustache tag placeholders contained in the template, this fitting pushes a single message output with the contents from the HTML template. If the Mustache references are not found in the input payload, the placeholders will be replaced with empty content.

Example

See First Integration Pipeline: Hello World for a sample of how to create a simple first pipeline from start to finish.

The HTML Formatter receives the following payload from the previous fitting in the pipeline:

{"message": {
  "header": {},
  "payload": {
    "headers": ["Fund", "Offered ($)"],
    "rows": [{"fund":"Federal Work-Study (FWS)",
              "offer":"$ 1,500"},
             {"fund":"Federal Perkins Loan",
              "offer":"$ 1,250"},
             {"fund":"Federal Stafford Loan - Subsidized",
              "offer":"$ 1,750"},
             {"fund":"Federal Stafford Loan - Unsubsidized",
              "offer":"$ 1,000"}]
    }
  }
}

The HTML Formatter template area is configured with the following HTML code and Mustache tag references:

<html><body>
<table>
<tr>
{{#message.payload.headers}}
<th>{{.}}</th>
{{/message.payload.headers}}
</tr>
{{#message.payload.rows}}
<tr>
<td>{{fund}}</td>
<td>{{offer}}</td>
</tr>
{{/message.payload.rows}}
</table>
</body></html>

The HTML Formatter parses the Mustache tags, iterates through the arrays, and finds the values for the expressions, generating the following HTML: 

<html><body>
<table>
<tr>
<th>Fund</th>
<th>Offered ($)</th>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Federal Work-Study (FWS)</td>
<td>$ 1,500</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Federal Perkins Loan</td>
<td>$ 1,250</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Federal Stafford Loan - Subsidized</td>
<td>$ 1,750</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<td>Federal Stafford Loan - Unsubsidized</td>
<td>$ 1,000</td>
</tr>
</table>
</body></html>

See Exercise III: HTML Formatter fitting example for a detailed example of the HTML Formatter fitting.

JavaScript Transform fitting

Use this fitting to write vanilla JavaScript to transform a message payload.

The JavaScript code can either be provided inline in the fitting configuration or retrieved from an external Transform Function. See Externalize JavaScript transform functions.

Expected input

A message of arbitrary type.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Code Optional. A transform function, properly escaped as a JSON string. Details of how the transform function is to be defined is given in next section.
Push Undefined Optional. Flag to allow fitting to push forward undefined messages, defaults to true.
Stop On Error Optional. If set to true, and the evaluated function throws an exception, this fitting will not process any further messages, effectively stopping the pipeline.
Artifact Name Optional. The name of a transformFunction type artifact (without the .js extension).
Artifact version Optional. A specific version of the transformFunction to retrieve, otherwise latest.

Transform function

   
Contract The JavaScript function must be named transform. It must accept at least one parameter, which is the message. It may accept a second parameter, which is the pipeline context. Values may be obtained from the pipeline context using context.get('key'). New values can also be added to the context from within a transform function by using the context.set function, which accepts a key and a value as parameters.
Note: The total amount of data stored in pipeline context — including values set using context.set() within a JavaScript Transform — is limited to 2.5 GB per execution. Exceeding this limit will cause the pipeline to fail with a clear error message.

The JavaScript function should always end with a return statement. The returned value will be pushed forward to the next pipeline segment. However, returning a message is not strictly required. Along with the pushUndefined configuration parameter value this fitting can be used to filter out messaged from the pipeline execution.

If the function throws an exception or external conditions throw an exception, for example an execution timeout, and the stopOnError flag is specified, any further messages will be dropped, effectively stopping the pipeline.

Example:

function transform (message, context) {
  // Put your code here.
  return message;
}
Note: If a JavaScript Transform deletes, sets to null, or sets to undefined the message.header or message.payload, you may see inconsistent message behavior at runtime. Avoid doing this; instead, update or overwrite specific fields.
Push undefined The pushUndefined flag defines what happens when transform functions don't return a message. When not set its value will be true by default, hence, if nothing is returned undefined will be forwarded. When pushUndefined is set to false and no message is returned from transform function, no message is forwarded to the next fitting.
Note: Allowing undefined messages to be forwarded may cause problems with subsequent segments.
Error handling If an error occurs with the transformation script due to code that is not valid, logical errors, or references that are not valid, the fitting will halt execution and no message will be pushed forward. All errors will be logged.

By default all scripts will have 30 seconds to execute. Code execution exceeding this time threshold will be halted and treated as an execution exception.

Transform function limitations

The function is executed in a sandbox, and may not require any modules.

Transform function caching

Artifact based scripts and inline code functions are compiled and cached for faster repeated execution. In the case of artifact based scripts, retrieval happens only one time per pipeline execution.

Output

The message pushed forward will totally depend on what the transformation function does. Output type is arbitrary unless the resulting object has a payload property in which case the fitting will automatically convert it to a Message object.

JSON Parser fitting

Use this fitting to parse a JSON string into a JSON object.

Expected input

The fitting accepts any type of incoming message, but will only parse one that has a JSON string payload.

Reference configuration

There are no required configuration fields.

Output

This fitting pushes a message for each incoming message. If the input payload was a JSON string, the output payload is a JSON object. If an error occurs during parsing, the message payload is unchanged.

Line Parser fitting

Use this fitting to split an incoming message on newline characters.

Expected input

Input should be either a message with a payload or a plain string message.

Reference configuration

There are no required configuration fields.

Output

For each newline character encountered, a new message will be pushed. The payload will be the line accumulated preceding the newline. The header will be the header from the incoming message or blank if the incoming message was just a string.

Merge with context values fitting

Use this fitting to combine messages passing through the fitting with other data residing in pipeline context based on a common key.

Expected input

Input should be a message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Context Property Required. The name of a property in context. The value must be an array.
Match On Required. Single or multiple property names which will be used to match the incoming record to a record in the context array.

Output

The incoming message is pushed back into the pipeline with a payload that may include additional properties from the data set in context.

Merge with context values fitting example

Given the value of the incoming message payload matchOn property, the array of data in pipeline context is searched for an object that has a matching value in the corresponding matchOn property.

If a match is found, all enumerable properties from the match are assigned to the incoming message payload. Existing properties will be overwritten. If multiple matches are found, the first will be used.

matchOn can hold a single property as a string or multiple properties as a string array.

For example, if the configuration is:

  • Context Property: arr

  • Match On: id

And the content entry arr is:

[
  {
    "id": "2",
    "foo": "zzz"
  },
  {
    "id": "1",
    "foo": "baz",
    "some": {
      "garbage": "here"
    }
  }
]

And the incoming message payload is:

{
  "id": "1",
  "foo": "bar"
}

Then the expected message that will be pushed as payload output will be:

{
  "id": "1",
  "foo": "baz",
  "some": {
    "garbage": "here"
  }
}
Object Mapper fitting

Use this fitting to map an object structure into another structure. The mapper uses JSONPath to look for values on a payload object, then transfer them to a target object property.

Expected input

A message with a header and a payload of type object or array. Payloads that are not of type object or array will be passed through as is with no mapping execution.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form: Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition are common to all fittings.

Configuration Description
Ignore Undefined Optional. Flag to enable or disable undefined or null mappings. When true, undefined and null values will not be added to the final mapped object.
Keep Original Optional. Flag to enable or disable the transferring of all source payload properties to the mapped object. Defaults to true.
Mappings Mappings rules allows you to look for information in a source object, optionally transform it, and put it in the mapped object. At least one mapping rule is required.
Crosswalk Optional. Crosswalks are a way to customize the translation of one value to another. These are Object Mapper specific crosswalks, not to be confused with tenant crosswalks.
Definitions Optional. Re-usable sets of mapping rules. They are useful when a mapping source data is a list of objects that needs to be broken down into sub-mappings.

Mappings

Configuration Description
Sources Required. Source locations to be queried to get the value that's going to be placed in the target. At least one source is required. It requires to have a path or default value or both.
Path JSONPath location of a specific data field within incoming payload. For example: $.student.id.
Default Value and Type Literal value to be used as source. When combined with a path the default value is used as fallback when path query results in undefined. The type allows you to specify how the default value should be used: as string (default), number, or Boolean. Default value can also make reference to message header or payload, context fields, or already mapped values by using mustache like references. Example: {{message.payload.field}}, {{message.header.field}}, {{context.year}}, or {{mapped.studentId}}.
Prevent path value reduction In the event where the path maps to a list with multiple values, the mapper will always use the first element in the list. If the intention is to use the whole list, switch on this flag to prevent the default reduction.
Target Defined where the source value is going to be placed.
Name Dot-notation path of where the source value is going to be placed in the mapped object.
Target is a Mapped List Optional. Flag to identify if the source value is a list of objects that needs further mapping. The switch only becomes available when there are defined definitions. When switched on the Mapping Definition field is made available.
Mapping Definition Definition to be used to map the source's list of objects. The values available in this list are directly related to the Object Mapper's definitions.
Transformation Functions Optional. Series of transformation functions applied to the queried source value. When more than one function is specified the series is executed in the order in which they are listed. The source value will always be automatically sent as a parameter to the functions.
Category and Function Refer to the Transformation functions list to see available functions.
Parameters Optional. List of additional parameters to be sent to the selected function. Not all functions require additional parameters.

Definitions

Configuration Description
Name Name used to identify the definition. This name would be available in the target's mapping definition drop-down.
Mappings Definition mappings rules allows you to look for information in a source object, optionally transform it, and put it in the mapped object. Configure these mappings just like top level Object Mapper mappings.

Output

This fitting pushes a new message with the same header as the incoming message.

When the incoming payload is of type object or array, the new message payload will be the mapped outcome. Otherwise, message payload will be passed through.

Transformation functions

There are several transformation categories each of which contain one or more functions that can be used to change a mapped field's format or content.

string

  • toUpper: Converts all the alphabetic characters in a string to uppercase.
  • toLower: Converts all the alphabetic characters in a string to lowercase.
  • trim: Removes the leading and trailing white space and line terminator characters from a string.
  • truncate: Truncates a string if it exceeds a specified maximum length. Accepts one numeric parameter.
  • trimTruncate: Removes the leading and trailing white spaces and truncates a string if it exceeds the specified maximum length. Accepts one numeric parameter.
  • append: Appends one or more values to the input and returns the result.
  • prepend: Prepends one or more values to the input and returns the result.
  • substr: Gets a substring beginning at the specified location and having the specified length.
  • replace: Replaces text within input using a regular expression or search string.
  • split: Split a string into substrings using the specified separator and return them as an array.
  • toNumber: Converts a string value into a number.

number

toFixed: Returns a string representing a number in fixed-point notation. Accepts one numeric parameter.

date

format: Converts a date from an input format to the output format. Accepts 2 parameters, an input and an output date format strings. Based on moment.js format tokens.

array

  • unique: Returns a duplicate free version of list. Only works for primitive data types like strings and numbers, and is case sensitive. Aliases: removeDuplicates
  • without: Return an array version without provided values.
  • join: Adds all the elements of an array separated by the specified separator string. Accepts an optional delimiter parameter. If omitted, comma (,) is used to join array values.
  • find: Returns the value of the first element in the array where criteria or pathExpression predicate is true. For example, preferred as criteria and $.preference as pathExpression.

object

  • get: Returns the value of the first element matching pathExpression.
  • query: Returns an array of elements that satisfy the provided JSONPath expression, or an empty array if none were matched.

util

  • crosswalk: Translates the values in a single string or array based on crosswalk. Accepts one string parameter to specify which crosswalk configuration or function to use.
  • coalesce: Returns specified alternate value when input is undefined or null.
  • log: Outputs input content to console.log and passes-through its value. Used primarily for debugging purposes.

Crosswalks are a way to customize the translation of one value to another. This is especially useful when data need to match a very specific set of enumerated values. When using util.crosswalk, you can reference tenant wide crosswalks or segment defined ones. The name of the crosswalk needs to be set as the first function parameter. If the crosswalk is not found the function will not be executed and ignored.

There are some built-in crosswalk functions that can be used out of the box with util.crosswalk:

  • iso3166.country.alpha3ToAlpha2 : Converts an ISO 3166-1 Country Code from Alpha-3 to Alpha-2.
  • iso3166.country.alpha2ToAlpha3 : Converts an ISO 3166-1 Country Code from Alpha-2 to Alpha-3.
  • hashmap.getValue : Returns the value of a given hashmap key. Uses the transformation input as key and requires a hashmap to be sent as input.
Mapping examples

All examples use the same input payload data.

{
  "greetings": [
    { "content": "What's up?", "type": "i" },
    { "content": "How are you?", "type": "f" }
  ]
}

Simple mapping

This is a simple and straightforward example with just 2 mappings:

  • $.greetings.0.content into message
  • $.greetings.0.type into type

Fitting configuration:

  • Mapping01:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.content
    • Target -> Name: message

  • Mapping02:

    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.type
    • Target -> Name: type

The resulting payload should be:

{
  "message": "What's up?",
  "type": "i"
}

Mapping with multiple source paths

The following example builds upon the previous example configuration. In this case, the Mapping 2 rule will be expanded to look for paths $.greetings.0.code and $.greetings.0.type, to then map it to type.

When there are multiple source paths, each one will be queried sequentially in the order in which they are listed. The first query to render data that is not undefined will prevail as the source.

Fitting configuration:

  • Mapping01:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.content
    • Target -> Name: message

  • Mapping02:

    • Sources01 -> Path: $.greetings.0.code
    • Sources02 -> Path: $.greetings.0.type
    • Target -> Name: type

The resulting payload should be:

{
  "message": "What's up?",
  "type": "i"
}

Notice that type is still "i". Because $.greetings.0.code does not exist in the greeting data object, it queries the next path in the sequence $.greetings.0.type.

Mapping with transformation

The following example builds upon the previous example configuration. In this case, the Mapping 1 rule will contain a string.toUpper transformation.

Fitting configuration:

  • Mapping01:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.content
    • Target -> Name: message
    • Transformation Functions -> Category: string
    • Transformation Functions -> Function: toUpper

  • Mapping02:

    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.type
    • Target -> Name: type

The resulting payload should be:

{
  "message": "WHAT'S UP?",
  "type": "i"
}

Notice that the mapped message, instead of the original "What's up?" value, is in upper case now due to the transformation.

Mapping with multiple transformations

The following example builds upon the previous example configuration. In this case, the Mapping 1 rule will contain an additional transformation: string.replace. The transformation will be placed right after the string.toUpper.

When there are multiple transformations, each one is executed sequentially in the order in which they are listed. The first function receives the source as parameter automatically, any subsequent functions receive the output of the previous one as an automatic parameter.

Fitting configuration:

  • Mapping01:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.content
    • Target -> Name: message

    • TransformationFunctions01:

      • Category: string
      • Function: toUpper

    • TransformationFunctions02:

      • Category: string
      • Function: replace
      • Enter Parameters: UP - DOWN (Click the + button after entering each parameter.)
  • Mapping02:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.type
    • Target -> Name: type

The resulting payload should be:

{
  "message": "WHAT'S DOWN?",
  "type": "i"
}

Notice that the mapped message, instead of the original "What's up?" value, is converted to upper case: "WHAT'S UP?". Finally, a replace operation is executed to find the word "UP" and convert it to "DOWN."

Mapping with crosswalk

The following example builds upon the previous example configuration. In this case, the Mapping 2 rule will contain a util.crosswalk transformation making reference to the greetingType crosswalk definition.

Fitting configuration:

  • Mapping01:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.content
    • Target -> Name: message
    • TransformationFunctions01:
      • Category: string
      • Function: toUpper
    • TransformationFunctions02:
      • Category: string
      • Function: replace
      • Enter Parameters: UP - DOWN (Click the + button after entering each parameter.)
  • Mapping02:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.0.type
    • Target -> Name: type
    • Transformation Functions -> Category: util
    • Transformation Functions -> Function: crosswalk
    • Transformation Functions -> Enter Parameters: greetingType (Click the + button after entering the parameter.)

And the following crosswalk definition:

  • Crosswalk Name: greetingType
  • Mapping01:
    • Target Value: Informal
    • Source Value: i
  • Mapping02:
    • Target Value: Formal
    • Source Value: f

The resulting payload is:

{
  "message": "WHAT'S DOWN?",
  "type": "Informal"
}

Notice that the mapped type, instead of the original "i" value, has been translated into "Informal" based on the util.crosswalk transformation.

Mapping with definition

For this example, instead of mapping the first greeting in the list, we're going to target them all in just one mapping rule by using a definition.

Fitting configuration:

  • Mappings:
    • Sources -> Path: $.greetings.*
    • Target -> Name: greetings
    • Target -> Target is a mapped list: ON
    • Target -> Select Mapping Definition: greeting
  • Crosswalk:
    • Crosswalk Name: greetingType
    • Mapping01:
      • Target Value: Informal
      • Source Value: i
    • Mapping02:
      • Target Value: Formal
      • Source Value: f
  • Definitions:
    • Name: greeting
    • Mapping01:
      • Sources -> Path: $.content
      • Target -> Name: message
      • Transformation Functions -> Category: string
      • Transformation Functions -> Function: toUpper
    • Mapping02:
      • Sources -> Path: $.type
      • Target -> Name: type
      • Transformation Functions -> Category: util
      • Transformation Functions -> Function: crosswalk
      • Transformation Functions -> Enter Parameters: greetingType (Click the + button after entering the parameter.)

The resulting payload is:

{
  "greetings": [
    { "message": "WHAT'S UP?", "type": "Informal" },
    { "message": "HOW ARE YOU?", "type": "Formal" }
  ]
}

Notice that the payload now is a greetings field with an array of mapped greeting objects.

When mapping a list of elements using definitions, the current index and length of the list can be accessed using mustache style references to {{array.index}} and {{array.length}} respectively. These can be useful to set default IDs to each element.

Run Ruleset fitting

Use this fitting to execute a ruleset on a record or batches of records.

Expected input

A message with a payload of type object or array is required for ruleset execution. Payloads that are not objects or arrays will be passed through as-is, without triggering any ruleset execution.

To perform a ruleset batch evaluation, ensure that the data source is contained within a JSON attribute. If the payload is a direct array, Data Connect splits it into separate messages, each containing a single record, and each record will be evaluated independently. If that payload contains multiple records (not in an array), then the fitting performs an single evaluation for one record at a time.

Example message.payload batch evaluation:

{
  "data": [
    { "name": "Viktor", "lastName": "Frankenstein", "age": 30 },
    { "name": "Agatha", "lastName": "De Lacey", "age": 20 },
    { "name": "Elizabeth", "lastName": "Lavenza", "age": 22 }
  ]
}

Example message.payload single evaluation:

{ name:"Viktor", lastName:"Frankenstein", age: 30 }

Passed through payloads (no mapping):

message.payload = 'foo bar';
message.payload = 3.14;
message.payload = true;

Reference configuration

Configure the ruleset and mappings to be used for the evaluation.

Topic Reference
Ruleset Required. Configure the ruleset and mappings to be used for the evaluation.

Select a Ruleset option from the drop-down list of published rulesets. The publish status and version of the ruleset display.

Click View Ruleset to open the Ruleset builder page in View mode only. This is the page that displays in Integration Packages when you create and publish a rule. You can test the ruleset here. You need to set up permissions. See Test and publish a Data Connect ruleset.

Map Values

Disabled until a ruleset is selected. When a ruleset is selected, the Map Values field retrieves the elements that are part of the ruleset and displays them as Unmapped values. You must map at least one of those values or you will receive an error.

Click Map Values to edit a mapped value.

The Batch Evaluation toggle default setting is On. Enabling this evaluates records in a batch.

When Batch Evaluation is On, the Source field is required to indicate where the data is in the payload to evaluate. Add a JSONPath for the object that contains the data to evaluate. For example: $.rulesetData[*]

When you toggle Batch Evaluation to Off, you can process a single record using the regular ruleset evaluation API.

To enter the Mapped value, enter a static value or a dynamic JSONPath expression for the fact in the payload. For example: $.employeeTenure. Enter map values for each of the ruleset elements.

If you leave Mapped value blank, then an empty value is evaluated for reference and treated as empty.

Accepted data types are string, number, boolean, and date.

To accommodate the various time zones, always use this ISO format for a static date: YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00.000Z
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put the evaluation response. When the target is not set, it replaces the whole message payload.
Ignore Errors Optional. Disabled by default. Flag that when set to true disables error reporting to Ethos Integration when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this pushes the original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in the header or payload.

Expected configuration

{
  "class": "runRuleset",
  "config": {
    "ruleset": "object",
    "namespace": "string",
    "mapValues": [ /* List of payload field mapping rules */ ],
    "target": "string", // Optional - Dot-notation target within payload to put the evaluation response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload.
    "errorPath": "string", // Optional - Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.
    "ignoreErrors": "boolean" // Optional flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
  }
}

Considerations

Consider the following when executing a ruleset:
  • Users can only create the Run Ruleset fitting using a ruleset in Published status.
  • If the selected ruleset for the fitting changes from Published to Outdated, it can still be evaluated. However, it will not be evaluated if its status is Archived.
  • If an Outdated ruleset is set on the Run Ruleset fitting, a pipeline developer needs to select Create Draft to create a draft pipeline, select a Published ruleset in the draft Run Ruleset fitting, and configure mappings. The developer can still save, test, and publish a pipeline if a Run Ruleset fitting has an Outdated ruleset.
  • If an Archived ruleset is set on the Run Ruleset fitting, a pipeline developer needs to select Create Draft to create a draft pipeline, select a Published ruleset in the draft Run Ruleset fitting, and configure mappings. The developer can still save a pipeline, but cannot test and publish a draft pipeline if a Run Ruleset fitting has an Archived ruleset.
  • If the Target is set, the payload contains the incoming data from the previous fitting (for example, the rulesetData array from the JavaScript Transform fitting) and the evaluation API response in the custom target.
  • If the Target is not set, the payload contains only the evaluation API response.
  • If the Target is not set, the message.payload is overwritten.
  • If Ignore Errors is disabled and the entire evaluation fails, then the Run Ruleset fitting will fail and an error will be written to the error log. If an Error Path is set, any errors during the fitting execution will be written to the user-specified path.
  • If Ignore Errors is set to Enabled and the entire evaluation fails, then the Run Ruleset fitting will succeed and an error will not be written to the error log. If an Error Path is set, any errors during the fitting execution will be written to the user-specified path.
