Quick start

Configuration in its simplest form allows for:
  • the specification of the ruleset to be executed
  • mapped values
  • a target object property
  • error handling

Consider the following configuration intended for a batch execution:

{
  "class": "runRuleset",
  "config": {
    "ruleset": { "rulesetId": "e35499a2-cb50-41f3-a981-698ed2268c8d", "namespace": "data-connect" },
    "mapValues": [
      {
        "source": "$.data[*]",
        "group": "HR",
        "element": "demo-age",
        "dataType": "number",
        "mapValue": "$.age"
      },
      {
        "source": "$.data[*]",
        "group": "HR",
        "element": "demo-name",
         "dataType": "string",
        "mapValue": "$.name"
      }
    ]
  }
}

An array payload with value:

{
  "data": [
    { "name": "Viktor", "lastName": "Frankestein", "age": 30 },
    { "name": "Agatha", "lastName": "De Lacey", "age": 20 },
    { "name": "Elizabeth", "lastName": "Lavenza", "age": 22 }
  ]
}

Result:

[{
  batchEvaluationId: "f6f77130-91d4-429f-918f-8e54fb8c47b2",
  totalErrorCount: 0,
  evaluations: [
    {
      evaluationId: 1,
      inputs: [
        {
          fact: "demo-age",
          value: 30,
          group: "HR"
        },
        {
          fact: "demo-name",
          value: "Viktor",
          group: "HR"
        }
      ],
      outputs: [
        {
          Rule: 3,
          Value: "C"
        }
      ]
    },
    {
      evaluationId: 2,
      inputs: [
        {
          fact: "demo-age",
          value: 20,
          group: "HR"
        },
        {
          fact: "demo-name",
          value: "Agatha",
          group: "HR"
        }
      ],
      outputs: [
        {
          Rule: 3,
          Value: "C"
        }
      ]
    }
  ],
  ruleset: {
    rulesetId: "e35499a2-cb50-41f3-a981-698ed2268c8d",
    name: "TEST_COMPLEX_1C - a",
    version: "2.0.0",
    returnFirstMatchedRuleOnly: false
  }
}]
Based on the configured mapping:
  • $.data[*].name was found and mapped to fact demo-name
  • $.data[*].age was found and mapped to fact demo-age

An individual ruleset execution would expect an object in the payload. See the example of the configuration.

{
  "class": "runRuleset",
  "config": {
    "ruleset": { "rulesetId": "e35499a2-cb50-41f3-a981-698ed2268c8d", "namespace": "data-connect" },
    "mapValues": [
      {
        "source": "",
        "group": "HR",
        "element": "demo-age",
        "dataType": "number",
        "mapValue": "$.age"
      },
      {
        "source": "",
        "group": "HR",
        "element": "demo-name",
         "dataType": "number",
        "mapValue": "$.name"
      },
    ]
  }
}

An object payload with value: 

{ name:"Viktor", lastName:"Frankestein", age: 30 }

Result:

{
  evaluationId: 1,
  inputs: [
    {
      fact: "demo-age",
      value: 30,
      group: "Group"
    },
    {
      fact: "demo-name",
      value: "Viktor",
      group: "Group"
    }
  ],
  outputs: [
    {
      Rule: 3,
      Value: "C"
    }
  ],    
  ruleset: {
    rulesetId: "e35499a2-cb50-41f3-a981-698ed2268c8d",
    name: "TEST_COMPLEX_1C - a",
    version: "2.0.0",
    returnFirstMatchedRuleOnly: false
  }
}
Based on the configured mapping:
  • name was found and mapped to fact demo-name
  • age was found and mapped to fact demo-age

Output

The batch evaluation processes 500 records within a batch and is automatically built based on the input data.

This fitting pushes a new message for each batch execution result. If a target is specified it saves the result in the target provided. Otherwise the result is returned in the payload. The header remains the same as the incoming message.

When the incoming payload is of type object or array, the new message payload will be the outcome of the execution. Otherwise, the message payload will be passed through.

Message payload structure

The content of the evaluation API response output changes based on how many rules within the ruleset matched. The rule/value structure will stay the same, unless no rules matched, but how many of the rule/value pairs will depend on how many rules matched. The output is an array with some number of key/value pairs with a rule/value.

For example, for a ruleset that has three rules:

If no rules in the ruleset matched, the output contains:

[]

If one out of three rules in the ruleset matched, the output contains:

[
    {
      "Rule": 1,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 1"
    }
  ]

If two out of three rules in the ruleset matched, the output contains:

[
    {
      "Rule": 1,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 1"
    },
    {
      "Rule": 2,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 2"
    }
  ]

If three out of three rules in the ruleset matched, the output contains:

 [
    {
      "Rule": 1,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 1"
    },
    {
      "Rule": 2,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 2"
    },
    {
      "Rule": 3,
      "Value": "Result from Rule 3"
    }
  ]
SFTP Delete fitting

Use this fitting to perform a SFTP delete operation to delete a file.

If your Integration pipeline uses SFTP fittings, your firewall rules, or the firewall rules of a third party, may need to allow for inbound requests. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected input

Input should be an optional message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Private Key Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the private key used for authentication. This or password must be present. Takes priority over password if defined.
Password Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the password used for authentication. This or privateKey must be present. Ignored if privateKey is defined.
Username Required. Can be interpolated, for example, {{message.payload.username}} or {{context.username}}.
Host Required. The Host address to reach.
File Name Required. Path to the remote file to delete.
Port Optional. Default is 22. SFTP port supports Mustache expressions.

If the port is a number, use that number.

If the port is a Mustache expression, evaluate it. If it evaluated to a number, use that number instead of the default.

If the value is not a number or a Mustache expression, the value is not valid.

Output

Message received will be pushed as-is.

SFTP Delete fitting example

This configuration will pick up the required configuration values from the message payload.

  • Use: Private Key
  • Private Key: privateKey
  • Username: {{message.payload.username}}
  • Host: {{message.payload.host}}
  • File Name: {{message.payload.fileName}}

The following configuration uses the provided values:

  • Use: Private Key
  • Private Key: privateKey
  • Username: userName
  • Host: hostName
  • File Name: path/filename
Stringify fitting

Use this fitting to stringify a JSON payload.

Expected input

The fitting accepts any type of incoming message, but will only stringify one that has a JSON object payload.

Reference configuration

There are no required configuration fields.

Output

This fitting pushes a message for each incoming message. If the input payload was a JSON object, the output payload is a JSON string.

XML Formatter fitting

Use this fitting to generate an XML, based on a configured template using data from messages and context.

Expected input

The formatter expects each message payload to be an object. Payloads that are not of type object will be ignored by the fitting with no pass-through.

Reference configuration

The only required configuration field is template.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root>
  <Student *payloadLoop="true" *source="$.student" id="${source.id}">
    <Name>${source.name}</Name>
    <Course *source="$.courses">${source}</Course>
  </Student>
</Root>

A series of payloads:

// Payload 1
{ student: { name: 'John Smith', id: '100', courses: ['English', 'Spanish'] } }
// Payload 2
{ student: { name: 'Jane Doe', id: '200', courses: ['Calculus', 'Statistics'] } }

Will be formatted as:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root>
  <Student id="100">
    <Name>John Smith</Name>
    <Course>English</Course>
    <Course>Spanish</Course>
  </Student>
  <Student id="200">
    <Name>Jane Doe</Name>
    <Course>Calculus</Course>
    <Course>Statistics</Course>
  </Student>
</Root>

XML template

The XML template configuration allows you to define what the final XML should look like in the end. Along with special directives and interpolation placeholders data from messages and context can be integrated into the final outcome.

Well formed XML is required for the fitting to work as expected.

Declaration

An XML declaration (like the one below) is required only if the final XML needs it.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>

A valid scenario where a declaration can be ignored is when the fitting is used to generate XML fragments.

<Foo>Hello World</Foo>
<Bar>Bar 1</Bar>
<Bar>Bar 2</Bar>

You can see from the sample above the template lacks a declaration, and a root element.

Directives and interpolation can be used on XML fragments.

Directives

There are three directives that can be used in the template configuration: *source, *scope, and *payloadLoop. All directives are optional but crucial when mapping data.

  • *source: JSON path string to refine an element's data scope. All root elements have a default source of $.payload, which points to the Message.payload field. A parent's *source scope is passed to all its children as their default *scope. When a non-root element *source is not set, it will be defaulted to its *scope. The only way a deeply nested element can use a different Message field, like the Message.header, is to reset the scope with the *scope directive. The dollar sign ($) in a source's JSON path value always points to the inherited or set *scope.
  • *scope: JSON path string to define an element's message data scope. All root elements have a default scope of $, which is the Message root. Non-root (or nested) elements get their scope from its parent's *scope and *source combination. The dollar sign ($) in a scope's JSON path value always points to the Message object.
  • *payloadLoop: Boolean flag that defines an element as an element that will repeat based on each message received. There can only be one *payloadLoop per template. If more than one element is marked as *payloadLoop only the first one found (while doing a top-down document traverse) will be taken into consideration for looping.

All directives are used as attributes and are required to have the asterisk prefix, otherwise they will be considered a plain element attribute.

*source mappings that reference an array will cause an element to be automatically repeated.

Interpolation

Values from messages and context can be integrated into the final XML by using interpolation references. Interpolation references are dot-notation path strings wrapped with squiggly brackets and a starting dollar sign, that is ${source.name}. The references can be used within attributes, and element text (even within CDATA).

Interpolation paths can have two different root nodes: source and context.

  • source: References the inherited or defined element scope or source from processed Message object.
  • context: References the pipeline's Context object.

Interpolation paths should always point to primitive values such as string and numbers, but if an array is found values will be automatically joined with commas.

The interpolation reference ${source} can be used when the element source mapping produces an array of primitive values. The element will be repeated by each array item; the only way to reference each item's value is by using ${source}.

Sample interpolation paths:

  • ${source}
  • ${source.name}
  • ${source.address.city}
  • ${context.runId}

Static (or hard coded) content can be combined with interpolation to create richer XML content. For instance, and attribute or element content value of "RunId-${context.runId}" will render as "RunId-123456789", assuming the context's runId value is 123456789.

Example

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root>
  <Student *payloadLoop="true" *source="$.student" id="${source.id}">
    <Name>${source.name}</Name>
    <Course *source="$.courses">${source}</Course>
  </Student>
  <Transaction *scope="$.header">${source.transactionId}</Transaction>
</Root>

And the following message structure:

{
  header: { transactionId: 12345 },
  payload: {
    student: {
      name: 'John Smith',
      id: '100',
      courses: ['English', 'Spanish']
    }
  }
}

Based on template the following can be inferred for the <Root> element:

  • *scope is defaulted to $
  • *source is defaulted to $.payload
  • All of <Root> children's scope would point to $.payload
  • <Student> element:
    • *scope value is inherited from <Root>: $.payload
    • *source is explicitly set to $.student
    • *payloadLoop is set to true. Multiple instances of the element will be rendered if more than one message is processed by the fitting.
    • Attribute id has an interpolation reference: ${source.id}. This mapping is going to retrieve the id field from the element's source $.student.
    • All of <Student> children's scope would point to $.payload.student
    • <Name> element:

      *scope value is inherited from <Student>: $.payload.student

      • *source value is defaulted to element's scope: $.payload.student
      • Text has an interpolation reference: ${source.name}. This mapping is going to retrieve the name field from the element's source $.student.
      • All of <Name> children's scope would point to $.payload.student.
    • <Course> element:
      • *scope value is inherited from <Student>: $.payload.student
      • *source is explicitly set to: $.courses
      • Because <Course>'s source points to an array, the element will be repeated for all courses contained in the list.
      • Text has an interpolation reference: ${source}, which points to each $.courses element.
      • All of <Course> children's scope would point to $.payload.student.courses.
  • <Transaction> element:
    • Rendering of this element happens right after the last message is processed due to its preceding sibling's *payloadLoop directive.
    • *scope value is explicitly set to: $.header. This element's scope was supposed to inherit <Student>'s source, but it got overridden.
    • *source value is defaulted to element's scope: $.header
    • Text has an interpolation reference: ${source.transactionId}. This mapping is going to retrieve the transactionId field from the element's source $.header.
    • All of <Transaction> children's scope would point to $.header.
XML Parser fitting

Use this fitting to parse content from XML into objects based on configuration.

Expected input

The parser expects each stream message payload to be of type string. Non-string payloads will be ignored by the fitting with no pass-through.

Reference configuration

There are no required configuration fields. The minimum segment configuration needed to use this fitting is shown below.

Configuration Description
Definition Optional. Object structure that allows for generic or specific XML path mapping rules.
Message For Each Optional. List of element node XML paths. A message is pushed for each element in the XML that matches any of the paths in this list.

An XML like:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root xmlns="http://ellucian.com/some-ns" xmlns:t="http://tempuri.org/">
  <Foo bar="bar">Hello World</Foo>
</Root>

Will be parsed as object payload:

{
  Foo: {
    bar: 'bar',
    __text: 'Hello World'
  }
}

The parser will automatically ignore the XML declaration section, and any xmlns or xsi related attributes. It will also automatically map any element inner content to the __text field (including CDATA content). The name can be replaced with a more meaningful name in the definitions section.

Definitions

A definition allows XML paths mapping to be customized. From data type specifications, to different mapping names, and even element ignoring; a definition provides a flexible way of custom tailoring a message payload. The following aspects can be specified in a path definition:

Configuration Description
Definition Name Optional. Custom mapping name. By default element and attributes are mapped using the very same name used in the XML (sans schema prefix).
Ignore Optional. Ignore setting. Possible values: never, always, empty. If not specified, a value of never is defaulted. When always is set, the path will never be mapped to any message payloads. When empty is set, the path will not be included in the message payload only when an empty string value is found in the XML.
Flatten Optional. Object flattening flag. This applies only to element nodes (not attributes or text nodes). By setting flatten as true to an element, if it only contains text with no other attributes; instead of an object with a __text property, the node element will be assigned a string with the text content. Example: Instead of { Foo: { __text: 'Hello' } }, it will be { Foo: 'Hello' }. By default flatten is false.
Type Optional. Type Definition. Options are string, number, Boolean, date and array. If not specified, string is used as the default type. If number, Boolean or date is chosen additional values can be configured.
Implicit Decimals Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Numeric parameters that specifies how many decimal spaces a number must contain when implicit decimal point format is used. This is very common on legacy systems where space was of the essence. For example, the number 314 with 2 implicit decimal positions means that the number must be interpreted as 3.14.
Symbol Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Number symbol to be ignored when parsing a numeric field that would otherwise make the conversion to number not successful. For example, dollar signs ($), percent (%), or the pound sign (#).
Is Accounting Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Flag to identify a numeric field as an accounting type. This specifically deals with negative numbers enclosed in parenthesis rather than using the minus (-) sign.
Base Optional. Displayed when type number is selected. Number base (or radix). Possible values: 2, 8, 10, and 16 for binary, octal, decimal, and hexadecimal respectively. By default all numbers are expected to be Base 10 (decimal). When a base other than 10 is used, all other number format properties are ignored except numberSymbol.
True Value Optional. True Value Match. When specified, if the mapped value matches the trueValue string, the field value will be set to true. Setting this property is only allowed if type is set to Boolean.
False Value Optional. False Value Match. When specified, if the mapped value matches the falseValue string, the field value will be set to false.
is ISO 8601 Optional. Flag that enables date parsing using ISO 8601 compatible formats. Setting this property is allowed only if type is set to date.
Format Optional date format or formats. It allows for a single string or list of possible formats to be expected. Setting this property is allowed only if type is set to date.

The definitions object uses XML paths as keys. Here are some example definition setups:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root xmlns="http://ellucian.com/some-ns" xmlns:t="http://tempuri.org/">
  <t:Foo>
    <Bar id="1">Hello</Bar>
    <Bar id="2">World</Bar>
  </t:Foo>
  <Baz>That&apos;s all folks!</Baz>
</Root>

With the following configuration:

  • Definition01
    • Definition Name: :text
    • Name: context
    • Ignore: Never
    • Type: String
  • Definition02
    • Definition Name: Root/t:Foo/Bar
    • Name: bars
    • Ignore: Never
    • Type: Array
  • Definition03
    • Definition Name: Root/t:Foo/Bar/@id
    • Ignore: Never
    • Type: Number
    • Base: Decimal
  • Definition04
    • Definition Name: Root/Baz
    • Ignore: Always
    • Type: String

The following payload will be sent:

{
  Foo: {
    bars: [
      { id: 1, content: 'Hello' },
      { id: 2, content: 'World' }
    ]
  }
}

Important things to note in the generated payload:

  • Foo is named after the <t:Foo> tag. However, the t: prefix is automatically removed. This is the default behavior for element and attribute nodes.
  • bars gets the name from the Root/t:Foo/Bar definition, instead of using Bar from the element node.
  • The id field for each bars object is casted to number thanks to the Root/t:Foo/Bar/@id definition.
  • The content field for each bars object gets the name from the global definition :text. Definitions can be made less restrictive by creating a less specific XML path. A definition such as :text applies to all elements with text/cdata content in the XML. This can be done with attributes and element nodes as well, but use carefully to avoid unexpected results.
  • Element <Baz> is not mapped into the final payload thanks to the ignore value in the Root/Baz definition.

Message for Each property

When the messageForEach property is not configured the fitting will parse the whole XML and produce a single message with an object representation of the XML content. While this works fine for small XML files, when it comes to very big ones it is better to be more selective about what gets parsed.

When an XML path is added to the messageForEach property, as the name implies, a message will be pushed each time a matching element is finished parsing. This makes the XML parsing more streamlined, as data is pushed even before the XML is completely parsed. Furthermore, chunking the XML parsing also helps with memory management and execution performance.

Only specify element node paths in messageForEach. Paths pointing to attribute nodes don't work and will be ignored.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root xmlns="http://ellucian.com/some-ns" xmlns:t="http://tempuri.org/">
  <Foo>
    <Bar id="1">Hello</Bar>
    <Bar id="2">World</Bar>
  </Foo>
  <Baz>That&apos;s all folks!</Baz>
</Root>

With the following configuration:

Enter Message For Each: Root/Foo/Bar - Root/Baz (Click the + button after entering each parameter.)

And an XML file:

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root xmlns="http://ellucian.com/some-ns" xmlns:t="http://tempuri.org/">
  <Foo>
    <Bar id="1">Hello</Bar>
    <Bar id="2">World</Bar>
  </Foo>
  <Baz>That&apos;s all folks!</Baz>
</Root>

The following payloads will be sent:

// Message Payload #1
{
  Bar: { id: '1', __text: 'Hello' }
}

// Message Payload #1
{
  Bar: { id: '2', __text: 'World' }
}

// Message Payload #3
{
  Baz: { __text: 'That\'s all Folks!' }
}

About XML Paths

This fitting utilizes XML paths for definitions and messageForEach configuration. Even though they may look like XPath, their only similarity is that forward slash (/) is used to separate nodes. Follow these rules to create a successful path:

  • Paths are case sensitive, element and attribute nodes need to match the case in which they are used within the XML.
  • Always use the full node name when building the path, even when it has a namespace prefix.
  • Attribute nodes need to be prefixed with the at (@) symbol.
  • Element content such as text or CDATA is matched by the pseudo node :text.
  • Path matching is always relative. To ensure the highest level of specificity a full path must be configured.

Example

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8" standalone="yes"?>
<Root xmlns="http://ellucian.com/some-ns" xmlns:t="http://tempuri.org/">
  <Student name="John Smith" age="33">
    <Course id="1">Spanish - 101</Course>
    <Course id="2">English - 101</Course>
  </Student>
  <Course name="English" code="101">
    <Session id="1" days="MWF" time="1:00PM" />
    <Session id="2" days="MWF" time="3:00PM" />
  </Course>
</Root>

The following paths are supported:

  • Root/Student/Course - Maps only Course element nodes in Root/Student elements.
  • Course - Maps Course element nodes in Root/Student and the ones inside the Root element as well.
  • Root/Student/Course/@id - Maps the id attribute node of Root/Student/Course elements.
  • Course/@id - Maps the id attribute node of all Course elements within the XML.
  • @id - Maps the id attribute node of any XML element that should contain it.
  • Root/Student/Course/:text - Maps the Root/Student/Course element's escaped/non-escaped content node.
  • Course/:text - Maps the escaped/non-escaped content of all Course element nodes within the XML.
  • :text - Maps the escaped/non-escaped content of any element node within the XML.

Common errors to avoid

Remember that the XML paths implemented in this fitting are not, and were not meant to mimic, XPath. Avoid the following:

  • Prefixing paths with /, //, ., or ... It is not supported. The fitting will automatically remove these prefixes from paths that have them.
  • Adding filtering predicates. Any paths containing predicates will be ignored. A predicate is the square bracket section on the following XPath: /Root/Student/Course[@id='1']
  • Adding asterisk (*) wildcard for flexible matching. It is not supported.

Destinations

These fittings send data to an end state.

Create Zip File fitting

The Create Zip File fitting reads multiple files from Ellucian cloud storage, compresses them together, and writes the resulting compressed file back to Ellucian cloud storage.

Note: The Create Zip File fitting is currently a beta release for customers testing new functionality.

The Create Zip File fitting expects an array of file names to be fetched from the Data Connect S3 source, compresses the files, and then sends the compressed file to the Data Connect S3.

Expected input

Input is a message payload that is a JavaScript object.

json
{
  "class": "ZipFile",
  "config": {
    "fileNamePath": "string", //Required -  A JSON Path location must be an filename array in the payload which will be used as input to the fitting.
    "key": "string" //Required - Path to the file to write, will be overwritten if exists. Allows interpolation>"
  }
}

Example fitting configuration:

json
{
  "class": "ZipFile",
  "config": {
    "fileNamePath": "$.filePath", // payload.filePath = ['filename1', 'filename2', ....]
    "key": "output.zip"
  }
}

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form: Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition are common to all fittings.

Configuration Options Description
File Name Path Required. A JSON path to an array of file names in the payload that will be used as input to the fitting.
Output File Name Required. The zipped output file. This will be overwritten if it exists. Can be interpolated, for example, {{context.out}}.

Output

Output is a new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that is the output file name(key).

Example fitting output:

MESSAGE { payload : "output.zip" }
Create Zip File example

Follow this example to build a pipeline that reads multiple files from an Ellucian cloud storage, compresses them together, and writes the resulting compressed file back to Ellucian cloud storage.

About this task

This pipeline is comprised of several segments.

Procedure

  1. In Ellucian Experience, click the Integration Designer card.
  2. Select the Integration package this new pipeline will be in.
  3. If necessary, create a new package.
    1. To create a new package, go to the Integration Designer and click + in the Packages section.
    2. Create a unique name for the package.
    3. Optional: Add a description of the package contents.
    4. Click Save.
    5. Select the package you just created in the list of packages to continue.
  4. Create a new pipeline.
    1. In the Pipelines section of the Integration Designer, click + PIPELINE to create a new pipeline.
    2. Enter a unique name for the pipeline.
    3. Optional: Enter a description for this pipeline.
    4. Click Save to save the pipeline.
  5. Click the name of the new pipeline from the list.
  6. Configure a JavaScript Transform.
    1. Select JavaScript Transform from the Transformations menu to build the first fitting for this example.
    2. Enter JavaScript Transform for the Fitting Name.
    3. Set Push Undefined as On.
      This is a flag to allow the fitting to push forward undefined messages, and defaults to On.
    4. For this example, enter the following code snippet: 
      function transform (message, context) {
  // Put your code here.
  context.set('file1', 'abctext.txt')
  context.set('file2', 'abccsv.csv')
  message.payload = `What is Lorem Ipsum?
Lorem Ipsum is simply dummy text of the printing and typesetting industry. Lorem Ipsum has been the industry's standard dummy text as of the 1500s, when an unknown printer took a galley of type and scrambled it to make a type specimen book. It has survived not only five centuries, but also the leap into electronic typesetting, remaining essentially unchanged. It was popularised in the 1960s with the release of Letraset sheets containing Lorem Ipsum passages, and more recently with desktop publishing software like Aldus PageMaker including versions of Lorem Ipsum.

Why do we use it?
It is a long established fact that a reader will be distracted by the readable content of a page when looking at its layout. The point of using Lorem Ipsum is that it has a more-or-less normal distribution of letters, as opposed to using 'Content here, content here', making it look like readable English. Many desktop publishing packages and web page editors now use Lorem Ipsum as their default model text, and a search for 'lorem ipsum' will uncover many web sites still in their infancy. Various versions have evolved over the years, sometimes by accident, sometimes on purpose (injected humour and the like).
  return message;
}
  7. Configure a File Writer fitting.
    1. Click File Writer from the Destinations menu.
    2. Enter File Writer for the Fitting Name.
    3. Set Include total count to On.
      If set, it will include the total number of records written to the file in the result message.
    4. Set Generate Presigned URL to On.
      If set, it will create and include a pre-signed URL to the generated file in the result message.
  8. Configure a JavaScript Transform.
    1. Click JavaScript Transform from the Transformations menu.
    2. Enter JavaScript Transform1 for the fitting name.
    3. Set Push Undefined to On.
    4. For this example, enter the following code snippet: 
      function transform (message, context) {
  // Put your code here.
  message.payload = `name,date,count,description,replaces_product,approved
"Inflatable Elephant, African", 2013-09-23,5,"Found in Africa.
They live in dense forests, mopane and miombo woodlands, Sahelian scrub or deserts.",null,true
Large Mouse,2013-08-19,3,"A ""largish"" mouse",General Mouse,false`
  return message;
}
  9. Configure a File Writer fitting.
    1. Click File Writer from the Destinations menu.
    2. Enter File Writer1 for the fitting name.
    3. Set Include total count to On.
    4. Set Generate Presigned URL to On.
  10. Configure a JavaScript Transform.
    1. Click JavaScript Transform from the Transformations menu.
    2. Enter JavaScript Transform2 for the fitting name.
    3. Set Push Undefined to On.
    4. For this example, enter the following code snippet: 
      function transform (message, context) {
  // Put your code here.
  const 
      file1 = context.get('file1'),
      file2 = context.get('file2')
  message.payload.fileArray = [file1, file2]
  context.set('out', 'outputZipFile.zip')
  return message;
}
  11. Configure a Create Zip File fitting.
    1. Click Create Zip File from the Destinations menu.
    2. Enter Create Zip File for the fitting name.
    3. Enter $.fileArray for the File Name Path.
    4. Enter {{context.out}} for the Output File Name.
  12. Configure a File Reader fitting.
    1. Click File Reader from the Sources menu.
    2. Enter File Reader for the fitting name.
    3. Enter {{context.__pipelineName}}/{{context.__runId}}/{{context.out}} for the Key.
    4. Set Binary to On.
      This returns the file in binary format instead of string.
    5. Set Error if no File to On.
      This is a flag to generate an error (instead of a warning) if a file is not found on S3.
  13. Configure a File Writer fitting.
    1. Click File Writer from the Destinations menu.
    2. Enter File Writer2 for the fitting name.
    3. Enter FileWriter_{{context.out}} as the File Name.
    4. Set Generate Presigned URL to On.
Ethos Proxy Post fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation to post an Ethos resource through Ethos Integration.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example persons.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

You will see both /api and /qapi endpoints returned from the API Selector. QAPIs are not supported from Ethos Proxy Post at this time.

After you select the resource, the resource you selected and the Content Version and Accept version you selected are populated on the Ethos Proxy Post fitting page with the major version selected.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Content Version

Required. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.
Accept Version

Required. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.

You can enter in multiple accept versions in the fittings. However, you can not select multiple versions from the API Selector. You can still manually type in additional API versions.
Alternative Content Representation Optional. Alternative content representation.
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put Ethos response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload.
Body Path Optional. A JSON Path in the payload which will be used as the body of the post. If set but the path returns undefined, no operation will be done and the message will be pushed through.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error".
Api Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.

Example

The following is an example of how to use Ethos Proxy Post:

  1. In order for this fitting to work, an Ethos API key should be created as a parameter. Click the drop-down menu aside the pipeline name, select Edit Pipeline Settings, and add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the configuration.
  2. Configure the fitting by adding a valid resource, content and accept versions. For example:
    • Resource: instructional-methods
    • Content Version: 6
    • Accept Version: 6
  3. It will be necessary to add some input data for this example:
    {
  "abbreviation": "RD1",
  "title": "Recitation/Discussion",
  "id": "00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000000"
}

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that is the response. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

Ethos Proxy Put fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation to put an Ethos resource through Ethos Integration.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Resource

Required. Ethos resource, for example persons.

Enter the resource name here or click Select API to use the API Selector to find the resource. See Find an API with the API Selector.

Note: If you click Select API, the Search API Catalog page displays. If you select a new API, the resource name is populated with the Ethos Integration resource name on the page. If you do not select a new API, the resource name does not change on the page.
Content Version

Required. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.
Accept Version

Required. Version for Ethos resource, for example 12.

If you use the API Selector, this field automatically populates.

You can enter in multiple accept versions in the fittings. However, you can not select multiple versions from the API Selector. You can still manually type in additional API versions.
Alternative Content Representation Optional. Alternative content representation.
Id From Payload Required (if no Id from Context is defined). JSON Path to id within payload itself. Mutually exclusive from Id From Context. For example, $.person.id.
Id From Context Required (if no Id from Payload is defined). JSON Path to id within context. Mutually exclusive from Id From Payload. For example, $.guid.
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put Ethos response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload.
Body Path Optional. A JSON Path in the payload which will be used as the body of the request. If set but the path returns undefined, no operation will be done and the message will be pushed through.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag that when set to true, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with errorPath to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload, in other words: "error" is the same as "payload.error".
Api Key Optional. Name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified ethosApiKey will be used.
Allow concurrent Optional. If set, allows multiple threads to send PUT requests concurrently for each input message.

Output

A new message with the same header as the input and with a payload that is the response. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

When specifying the idFromPayload or idFromContext configuration properties but provided with JSONPath syntax that is not valid, the Ethos resource is not reached, the original input message passes along to the next fitting and an error gets reported.

Ethos Proxy Put fitting example

For this fitting to work, start by creating an Ethos API Key as a parameter.

Procedure

  1. Near the pipeline name, click the drop-down menu and select Edit Pipeline Settings.
  2. Add a new pipeline parameter named ethosApiKey. The name is reserved so it will always pick that parameter unless a different option is selected as the API key in the configuration.
  3. Configure the fitting. For example:
    Field Example selection or entry
    Resource persons
    Content Version 12
    Accept Version 12
    Get Id From Payload
    Id From Payload $.student.id
File Writer fitting

Use this fitting to write a file to Ellucian cloud storage, by default an Ellucian maintained AWS S3 bucket.

To specify a bucket of your choosing, use the bucket configuration property and include AWS credentials in the related properties.

Expected input

The fitting accepts a message with payload, string, or buffer. When a message with payload is received it will be automatically stringified.

Expected configuration

Configuration Description
File Name Path to file, will be overwritten.
Add Newline After Each Message If set, will append new line after each message.
Include Total Count If set, will include the total number of records written to the file in the result message.
Generate Presigned Url If set, will create and include a pre-signed URL to the generated file in the result message.
Bucket Optional. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an S3 bucket name, not needed if using Ellucian maintained AWS S3 bucket.
Access Key Id Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Access Key ID. Not needed if using Ellucian maintained AWS S3 bucket.
Secret Access Key Required if using the bucket option. The name of a parameter (context entry) containing an AWS Secret Key. Not needed if using Ellucian maintained AWS S3 bucket.
Write Immediately Optional. This allows users to write multiple files. If true, it creates a new file for every new message. addNewLineAfterEachMessage is ignored.
UTF Encoding If Write Immediately is set to true, this drop-down displays. Default value is UTF-8. The other option is UTF-16.

Output

Unless otherwise specified, the fitting will attempt to preserve the incoming message header and include it as the outgoing message header. Different configurations yield different payloads. For example:

Options Description Result
Include Total Count: Not set Generate Presigned Url: Not Set Will not push a message.
Include Total Count: Not set Generate Presigned Url: Set

Will push a message with the presigned URL as payload.

{ payload : 'https://example.s3.amazonaws.com/123/TestExample/ExampleRunId/example.txt&...' }
Include Total Count: Set Generate Presigned Url: Not Set

Will push a Message (Requires add Newline After Each Message to be set as well) 

{ payload : {"totalCount":42}} }

Specifying only:

include Total Count with NO add Newline After Each Message will not push a message.
Include Total Count: Set Generate Presigned Url: Set

Will push:

{
  payload : {
    "totalCount":42, 
    "presignedUrl":'https://example.s3.amazonaws.com/123/TestExample/ExampleRunId/example.txt&...'}
  }
}
Write Immediately: Set Generate Presigned Url: Not set, Include Total Count: Not set

Will push the original message.

{
  header: {
    ...original header properties
  },
  payload : {
    ...original message payload
  }
}
Write Immediately: Set Generate Presigned Url: Set, Include Total Count: Set

Will push: (add Newline After Each Message will be ignored):

{
  header: {
    ...original header properties,
    presignedUrl: 'https://example.s3.amazonaws.com/123/TestExample/ExampleRunId/example.txt&...',
    totalCount: 1
  },
  payload : {
    ...original message payload
  }
}
Write Immediately: Not set Generate Presigned Url: Set, Include Total Count: Set

Will push:

{ payload : { "totalCount":1, "presignedUrl":'https://example.s3.amazonaws.com/123/TestExample/ExampleRunId/example.txt&...'} } }
Add Newline After Each Message Generate Presigned Url: Not Set Will not push a message.
File Writer fitting key interpolation

File Name accepts interpolation tags that will take into account values in context.

Key value examples:

  • sample-file.txt - Simple hard coded value (no interpolation).

  • {{context.filename}} - Interpolated value from context.

  • sample-folder/{{context.filename}} - Combination of hard coded folder with interpolated file name from context.

HTTP Request fitting

Use this fitting to perform an HTTP operation.

If your Integration pipeline uses the HTTP fitting to call a custom API that is hosted on-premise only, not through Ethos Integration, your firewall rules should allow for inbound requests from a list of static IP addresses. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected input

A message payload that is a string or JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Method Optional. HTTP method (GET|POST|PUT|DELETE, etc .). Defaults to GET.
Uri Required. Path to the requested resource. for example, http://domain/path.
Target Optional. Dot-notation target within payload to put response body
Result Headers Optional. Dot-notation target within message to put response headers. When not set headers will be dropped silently. Valid examples: theHeaders, payload.theHeaders, header.theHeaders, message.payload.theHeaders, message.header.theHeaders. Note that if the response is an array, the headers will be saved into message.header.propName even if payload was specified as the place to save them. Repeated headers will be stored in an array value.
Cache Optional. Flag to enable or disable response caching (only for GET requests), defaults to false.
Stream Optional. Flag to enable or disable response streaming (only for GET requests). When streaming is enabled cache and target will not be supported and result headers are ignored.
Authorization Optional. Authorization specification. The authorization section allows someone to setup user name and password for basic authorization header setup. This will override any explicit authorization header specification at the headers section.
Headers Optional. Hash of key or value pairs to be sent as headers.
Body Optional. Body specifications.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos whenever an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling logic further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.

The uri, method, headers, body.content, authorization.username, and authorization.password configuration fields can be templated using Mustache, with properties from context, message.header, or message.payload.

The authorization section allows someone to setup username and password for basic authorization header setup. This will override any explicit authorization header specification at the headers section.

Ellucian recommends that interpolation is utilized in both username and password. We use mustache.js to interpolate values. Avoid hard coding sensitive access information in a pipeline's configuration.

Example

The following is an example of how to use HTTP request fitting to make OAuth calls with client-id and secret-key.

  1. Enter the following parameters:

    a.

    • Name: clientId
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Client ID
    • Required: Yes
    • Sensitive: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1

    b.

    • Name: clientSecret
    • Required: Yes
    • Sensitive: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1

    c.

    • Name: authUrl
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Authentication URL
    • Required: Yes
    • Type: String

    d.

    • Name: resource
    • Label Type: Single string value
    • Label: Resource
    • Required: Yes
    • Type: String
    • Min Length: 1
  2. Enter the following fitting configuration:
    • Fitting Name: getAuthToken
    • Method: POST
    • Uri: {{{context.authUrl}}}
    • Authorization Username: {{{context.clientId}}}
    • Authorization Password: {{{context.clientSecret}}}
    • Body Type: from-urlencoded
    • Body Content: JSON
    {
  "grant_type": "client_credentials",
  "resource": "{{{context.resource}}}"
}

    As shown interpolation with mustache has been used to indicate that the configuration values will be picked up from the parameters during runtime.

  3. Run the test to get the Authorization token from the access_token in the payload of the result. Use the following information in the required fields:
    • Client ID: enterYourClientID
    • Client Secret: enterYourClientSecret
    • Authentication URL: https://test/token
    • Resource: https://testcloud.com

Output

Non-Streamed Requests

By default HTTP Fitting Request response body is read as a whole (in one step) and sent down the pipeline in a message envelope using the same header as the incoming message. If the response is JSON, it will be parsed into a JavaScript object.

Streamed Requests

When streaming is enabled by using the stream parameter, the fitting splits the request response body and sends each chunk as it is received down the pipeline as string until all content is read. This is useful for big downloads.

Note:

Result headers are not populated when using the streaming options.

Reducer fitting

Use this fitting to accumulate the incoming messages until there are no more messages, and then push one single message back into the pipeline.

Expected input

One or more messages, each with a header and a payload. This fitting, unlike some other fittings, does not push a new message for each message processed. Therefore this fitting should likely appear at or near the end of a pipeline, as it inherently blocks the entire pipeline until it has processed all the messages.

Expected configuration

Configuration Description
accumulator Required. The property in the new payload upon which to set the accumulated array of payloads.

Output

The output should be a message containing the header from the very last message received and containing a payload that is an array of all the payloads received.

SFTP Put fitting

Use this fitting to perform an SFTP put operation to upload a file to a remote server.

If your Integration pipeline uses SFTP fittings, your firewall rules, or the firewall rules of a third party, may need to allow for inbound requests. See Whitelist the Data Connect IP addresses.

Expected input

The fitting accepts a message payload that is a string or buffer. Each message payload is written to the file as it is received.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Private Key Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the private key used for authentication. This or password must be present. Takes priority over password if defined.
Password Required. The name of a pipeline parameter which will contain the password used for authentication. This or privateKey must be present. Ignored if privateKey is defined.
Username Required. Can be interpolated, for example, {{message.payload.username}} or {{context.username}}.
Host Required. Can be interpolated, for example, {{message.payload.host}}" or {{context.host}}.
File Name Required. Path to the remote file to download. This field accepts static text like filename.txt or a mustache variable like {{{context.filename}}} or {{{msg.payload.filename}}} that points to the file.
Port Optional. Default is 22. SFTP port supports Mustache expressions.

If the port is a number, use that number.

If the port is a Mustache expression, evaluate it. If it evaluated to a number, use that number instead of the default.

If the value is not a number or a Mustache expression, the value is not valid.
Push If set, this fitting will push a message containing the filename that was put.

Output

By default, this fitting does not push any messages into the pipeline. The configuration option push can be set to push a message that has a payload property of fileName containing the filename that was put.

The target attribute is required to add the document as an attachment.

Utilities

Utilities fittings provide additional functionality to help you build more robust pipelines.

Execute Banner Job fitting

Use the Ellucian Execute Banner Job fitting to use the output from a Banner job in the rest of the Data Connect pipeline.

Only users who have ERP Type set as Banner see the Execute Banner Job fitting.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form: Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition are common to all fittings.

Configuration Description

API Key

The name of a pipeline parameter containing an alternate API key to be used for Ethos requests. When not specified, ethosApiKey is used by default.

Note: Use an Ethos API Key subscribed to the applications configured with the Banner Admin API and Banner Integration API. The underlying user associated with the API key/token should have Banner security granted to access Banner batch jobs that you run from Integration Designer.
Job Name

This job name must match the Banner job name.

Enter only Process, C, and Java job types.
Output File Name Required. Data Connect supports .lis files, .log files and can support other Banner output file formats. You can enter a Banner output file name if it differs from the .lis format.

The default Banner output file name is based on the job details: {{jobName}}_{{jobNumber}}.lis. Edit the name or change the file extension if a different file needs to be retrieved. Mustache expressions are supported.

Note: Some Banner file types are not supported.
Ignore Errors Optional. When flag is set to On, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional: Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push the original message forward with error details. The Error Path can specify a location in the header or payload. When no location is specified, it defaults to payload. In other words, error is the same as payload.error.
Payload Target Path Optional. The Dot-notation target within the payload to put the Ethos response. When not set it replaces the whole message payload.
Parameters

Values Mapped and Unmapped values display.

Parameters appear automatically after you enter your Banner job name. Setup is required in Ethos Integration. See Set up Ethos Integration to call Banner job parameters for instructions.

Click Edit to edit parameters. The Parameters page displays. After you enter the Job Name and open the Parameters page, the default values are pre-populated that were defined in Banner for the listed parameters.

Note: Date values must be in DD-MON-YYYY format.

Some parameters support multiple values. The plus icon displays for the parameters that support multiple values. Click the plus icon to add multiple rows.

Click Reset to reset the parameters to the default value, or if you have saved parameters, to reset them to the last saved value.

The   DELETE button is available if there is more than one value.

Output

The fitting returns a payload object comprised of a Banner report split into a string array. Empty elements in the string array "" represent new lines on the report.

Set up Ethos Integration to call Banner job parameters

You can set up Ethos Integration to call Banner job parameters.

Procedure

  1. Select Tools > Ethos > Integration and then select the environment where you want to perform this procedure.
    When you log into Ethos Integration for the first time, the Enhance Your Experience page displays. Decline or allow Ellucian to enable cookies to track your usage in Ethos Integration using Google Analytics.
  2. Select the tenant to which you want to add the configuration, and click Select.
  3. On the Ethos Integration header bar, click Applications.
  4. In the Create New App area, click From Catalog and click the Create App link for your catalog application.
    The Browse Catalog page displays.
  5. Search for Ellucian, select Ellucian Banner, and click Create App.
  6. On the Add Applications page, enter the information described below, and then click Next.
    Field Entry
    Application name Enter an application name. For example: Banner Business Process API.
    Description Optional. Enter a description for this application.
  7. Enter the information described below, and then click Next.
    Option Description
    Base URI The default location at which all of the application's APIs reside.

    Enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminAPI.ws/api, where <hostname> is the name of your WebLogic or Tomcat server, and <port> is the port on that server that you configured for the Banner Admin API.
    Base QAPI URI The QAPI endpoint URI.

    Enter https://<hostname>:<port>/BannerAdminAPI.ws/qapi
    The Add Subscriptions page displays.
  8. Click Skip.
    A message displays that your application has been successfully added and configured.
  9. Click Resources, search for Parameter-definition and verify that the Resource Owner (*multiple) is the application you just created. If not, edit the resource and change it to the one you created.
  10. After you verify that the Parameter-definition resource has the correct owner, select Platform Components and click View on the Data Connect Platform component.
    The Ethos Platform Component Overview page displays.
  11. Select the Credentials tab and search for the application you just created. If it does not exist, add it:
    1. Click the Add Credentials button.
    2. Select your application from the Resource Owner drop-down list.
    3. Enter the Username and Password you set when you created the application.
    4. In the Select a resource field, select any Ethos resource to which that user account has permissions in Banner. For example, persons.
      Ethos Integration uses that resource to validate the user credentials by confirming that the user account has access to at least one resource in Banner. After the credentials are validated, the application will have access to all resources for which the user account has been granted permissions.
    5. Click Add.

What to do next

You are now ready to call the Banner job parameters endpoint with the Banner token. See Execute Banner Job fitting.
Open AI Chat Completions fitting

Use the Open AI Chat Completions fitting to call the OpenAI API chat completion endpoint.

The Open AI Chat Completions fitting enables users to leverage results returned by OpenAI in their Data Connect pipelines. It is available for Experience Premium customers.

Tip: To take advantage of this fitting, users must have their own OpenAI accounts that they use to authenticate to the OpenAI API.

Reference configuration

The OpenAI fitting passes the parameters for an OpenAI API call to define the model (for example, gpt-3.5-turbo, gpt-4) and content for the system and user roles and other parameters, as defined below.

The first three fields in the form: Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition are common to all fittings.

Configuration Description
Messages

Required. A list of messages comprising the conversation.

Choose the role and add the content message. The possible values for roles include:
  • system
  • user
  • assistant

Provide a JSON Path to the message content.
Model Required. The ID of the model to use. The models that support a JSON response include:
  • gpt-4-1106-preview
  • gpt-3.5-turbo-1106
Target Optional. The Dot-notation target within the payload to put the OpenAI API response. When not set, it replaces the whole message payload.
User A unique identifier representing your end-user, which can help OpenAI to monitor and detect abuse.
Ignore Errors Optional. When the flag is set to On, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path

Error details, in case of failure.

Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push the original message forward with error details. The Error Path can specify a location in the header or payload. When no location is specified it defaults to payload. In other words, error is the same as payload.error.
OpenAI API Key Required. Name of a pipeline parameter that will contain the API key to be used by this fitting. When not specified, openaiApiKey is used.
Temperature Choose a sampling temperature between 0 and 2. Higher values, such as 0.8, result in more random output, while lower values, such as 0.2, make it more deterministic. OpenAI recommends that you adjust either this or Top P, not both.
Top P

An alternative to sampling with temperature, called nucleus sampling, where the model considers the results of the tokens with Top P probability mass. So 0.1 means only the tokens comprising the top 10% probability mass are considered.

OpenAI recommends altering this or Temperature, but not both.
Frequency Penalty A number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on their existing frequency in the text so far, decreasing the model's likelihood to repeat the same line verbatim.
Presence Penalty A number between -2.0 and 2.0. Positive values penalize new tokens based on whether they appear in the text so far, increasing the model's likelihood to communicate new topics.
Max Tokens The maximum number of tokens to generate in the chat completion. The total length of input tokens and generated tokens is limited by the model's context length.
N How many chat completion choices to generate for each input message. You are charged based on the number of generated tokens across all the choices. Keep N as 1 to minimize costs.
Response Format

An object specifying the format that the model must output.

The JSON setting enables JSON mode and guarantees the message the model generates is valid JSON.

The Raw Text setting returns the content as text in the response object by default.

Output

The fitting will return a chat completion object. See details here: https://platform.openai.com/docs/api-reference/chat/object. This object can then be used in the context of the Data Connect pipeline.

Send Notification fitting

Use the Send Notification fitting to send email and or notifications to Experience from a Data Connect pipeline.

The Send Notification fitting sends a single email; to a maximum of 50 addresses; including To, Cc, and Bcc addresses.

The fitting sends the notification to the Notifications icon in Experience and to the user's mobile device. This notification will be generated for the Ethos Person GUID of the person who is configured in the fitting.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form: Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition are common to all fittings.

You must define and verify an email address before a user can use it to send emails. See Set up sender emails in the Ellucian Communicate documentation.

Configuration Description

Channels

The user is required to specify the email or notifications settings, but not necessarily both.

Email. Configure email sender, recipients, and content.

Enter the Email Details.

Required. From Address. Select an email address from those that display in the menu or select Use dynamically generated address.

If you select Use dynamically generated address, enter a variable from address using Mustache syntax.

Required. Enter To: Email Address(es).

Note: Enter email addresses or Mustache syntax one at a time and click the button.

Optional. Enter a Cc: and Bcc: email address or add the Mustache syntax.

Mustache usage:
  • For values containing HTML, such as <p>email@elucian.com</p>, triple braces {{{ }}} must be used to prevent special characters from being escaped, allowing the HTML to render correctly. For example: {{{msg.payload.email}}}.
  • For values without HTML, such as email@ellucian.com, it is sufficient to use double braces {{ }}, ensuring the content is properly escaped and not interpreted as HTML. For example: {{context.email}} or {{msg.payload}} or {{message.payload}}.
  • For To/Cc/Bcc fields, the Mustache variable can be a list. For example {{msg.payload.emails}}, where emails is a list of emails.

Required. Subject

Required. Enter Email Content.

Specify Text or HTML for the email body content.

Mustache usage:
  • For values containing HTML, such as <p>Hello</p>, triple braces {{{ }}} must be used to prevent special characters from being escaped, allowing the HTML to render correctly. For example: {{{value}}}.
  • For values without HTML, such as Hello, it is sufficient to use double braces {{ }}, ensuring the content is properly escaped and not interpreted as HTML. For example: {{value}}.

Enter content in the Email Content field.

Select the I acknowledge that Ellucian is not responsible for the content of Email check box.

Optional. Turn Add Attachments toggle to On to add attachments to the email. Steps 1 and 2 must be completed before this can be enabled. If enabled, at least one attachment is required.

Email and attachments are limited to 5 MB in total.

Enter the following:
  • File contents: Start with $. to call the message payload and the location of the file content string. For example: $.fileTest. File contents can use nested properties from the payload, something like $.level1.level2.testFile.
  • File Name with extension: Enter a file name or mustache expression. For example, {{message.fileName}}
  • Click + Add to add more attachments, as needed.

Notification. Configure notification recipient and content.

Click the Add Notification button. The fields on the Notification page include:
  • Required. Ethos Person GUID.
  • Required. Notification Title. Character limit is 50.
  • Required. Notification Text. Character limit is 125.
  • Optional. Include a Push Notification. Send push notification to the user's mobile device.
Target Optional. The Dot-notation target within the payload to put the Ethos response. When it is not set, it replaces the whole message payload.
Ignore Errors Optional. When the flag is set to On, it disables error reporting to Ethos when an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional: The Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push the original message forward with error details. The Error Path can specify a location in the header or payload. When no location is specified, it defaults to payload. In other words, error is the same as payload.error.

Output

The fitting returns a payload object for every channel option specified, such as a message ID, email send status, and notificationId. The target attribute is required to add the document as an attachment.

Sub-pipeline fitting

Use the Sub-pipeline fitting within an integration pipeline to run from another integration pipeline.

Use the Sub-pipeline fitting to select the sub-pipeline to be run at that step in the pipeline.

See Develop pipelines for a detailed description of pipelines and sub-pipelines.

Reference configuration

The first three fields in the form, Fitting Name, Fitting Description, and Fitting Execution Condition, are common to all fittings.

Context is shared between the parent pipeline and sub-pipeline; the appropriate way to set context variables using an Add to Context fitting or a JavaScript Transform fitting is context.set('value', 'string').

The Execution Condition from the Sub-pipeline fitting is added behind the scenes to all the fittings in the sub-pipeline.

Configuration Description
Sub-pipeline Define the sub-pipeline name. It must be unique on a global level. It cannot exist elsewhere with the same name in another tenant.
Version When Sub-pipeline is selected, the major version of the sub-pipeline that will be run as part of the execution of the integration pipeline in Experience Integration Packages is required.
Allow definition at job setup

When selected, the sub-pipeline is considered extensible. This allows you to select the sub-pipeline within the Pipeline Parameters tab in Integration Packages.

The value of defining a sub-pipeline at job definition is to allow the pipeline to use different sub-pipelines, depending on the job.

When selected, a sub-pipeline and version are not required. When the pipeline developer tests the parent pipeline in the Designer, the fitting will not do anything except pass the previous fitting message original payload.

Input

The output from the prior fitting (in the main pipeline) is passed as the message to the first fitting in the sub-pipeline.

Output

The output from the last fitting in the sub-pipeline is passed as the message to the next fitting in the main pipeline.

The payload is passed into the sub-pipeline as if it were the initial pipeline. The payload state at the end of the sub-pipeline returns back into the initial pipeline.

Insights transformations

These fittings can only be used with accounts that have the Insights Enterprise Extensibility license assigned.

Add Index fitting

Use this fitting to add a b-tree index to an existing table to improve reporting performance.

This fitting is only available for accounts with an Insights Enterprise Extensibility license.

Expected input

A message payload which is a JavaScript object.

Expected configuration

Configuration Description
Index Name Required. Name for the index.
Table Name Required. The name of the table to add index to.
Table Columns Required. An array of column names for the index.
Unique Optional. Indicates whether the column values will be unique for each row in the table.
Drop Optional. Indicates whether the index should be dropped from the table.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos whenever an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling logic further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.

Output

This fitting pushes a message into the pipeline. The output payload is a JSON object.

Example of the fitting executed successfully:

{
  "message": "Added index <schema>.<indexName>"
}
Add Primary Key fitting

Use this fitting to add a primary key constraint to an existing table.

This fitting is only available for accounts with an Insights Enterprise Extensibility license.

Expected input

A message payload which is a JavaScript object.

Expected configuration

Configuration Description
Constraint Name Required. Name for the primary key.
Table Name Required. The name of the table to add primary key to.
Table Columns Required. An array of column names for the primary key.
Drop Optional. Indicates whether the primary key should be dropped from the table.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos whenever an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling logic further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.

Output

This fitting pushes a message into the pipeline. The output payload is a JSON object.

Example of the fitting executed successfully:

{
  "message": "Added primary key constraint <constraintName> to table <schema>.<tableName>"
}

Additional information

  • All functions are created with the "STABLE" volatility classification. See https://www.postgresql.org/docs for more information.
  • The Argument Statement must contain a valid CREATE FUNCTION argument expression.
  • Any expression valid as a return data type in a CREATE FUNCTION statement can be used as the Return Type.
  • The SQL Statement must contain a valid PL/pgSQL block.
  • Dynamic SQL is not allowed in the PL/pgSQL block.

​Use this fitting to create a database function based on the supplied logic in the SQL block.

Expected input

​A message payload which is a JavaScript object. ​

Expected configuration

Configuration Description

  • SQL Statement:

    ...;
END;

{

}

Additional information
