Delete Data fitting

Use this fitting to delete records from a table in the custom_insights schema based on a specific condition.

This fitting deletes only the rows that match the configured condition and is commonly used to support incremental data refresh patterns.

Expected input

A message payload which is a JavaScript object.

Reference configuration

Configuration Description
Fitting Name Required. The name of the fitting instance.
Fitting Description Optional. The description of the fitting.
Fitting Execution Condition Optional. Determines whether the fitting executes.
Table Name Required. The name of the table in the custom_insights schema. Supports Mustache expressions.
Delete Condition Required. The condition used to determine which rows are deleted. Supports Mustache expressions.
Max Rows Optional. The maximum number of rows that may be deleted. Must be a whole number greater than or equal to 1.
Ignore Errors Optional. If enabled, the pipeline continues execution when an error occurs.
Error Path Optional. The path where error details are written when Ignore Errors is enabled.

Table Name

Specifies the table from which records are to be deleted.
  • Must exist in the custom_insights schema.
  • Supports Mustache parameter substitution.
For example:
canvas_course_activity
{{context.target_table}}

Delete Condition

Defines which rows are deleted.
  • Behaves like a SQL WHERE clause
  • Must be a valid SQL condition
  • Supports Mustache parameter substitution

For example:

id = 1
status = 'inactive'
academic_period = {{context.term_code}}
academic_period IN ({{context.periods}})
status = 'active' AND academic_period = {{context.term_code}}

Max Rows

Specifies the maximum number of rows that may be deleted.

  • Must be a whole number greater than or equal to 1
  • If the number of matching rows exceeds this value, the operation fails and no rows are deleted

This parameter is intended as a safeguard against large unintended deletions.

Ignore Errors

Controls pipeline behavior when an error occurs.

  • Off (default): pipeline fails
  • On: pipeline continues execution

Error Path

Defines where error details are written when Ignore Errors is enabled.

  • Uses dot notation
  • Stores error information in the message

For example:

payload.deleteError

Mustache parameter support

The following fields support Mustache expressions.

  • Table Name
  • Delete Condition

Parameters can reference values from:

context
message

For example:

"deleteCondition": "academic_period = {{context.term_code}}"

Example configuration

{
  "pipelineName": "Delete Current Term Data",
  "segmentName": "Delete Canvas Current Term",
  "class": "deleteData",
  "config": {
    "schema": null,
    "tableName": "canvas_course_activity",
    "deleteCondition": "academic_period = {{context.term_code}}",
    "maxRows": 500000
  }
}

Execution Behavior

When the fitting runs:
  1. The delete condition is evaluated
  2. Matching rows are identified
  3. If the number of rows exceeds Max Rows, the operation fails
  4. Otherwise, matching rows are deleted
  5. The pipeline continues to the next step

Output

This fitting pushes a message into the pipeline. The output payload is a JSON object.

For example:

{
  "message": "Deleted records from custom_insights.canvas_course_activity"
}

For an example use case, see

Incremental refresh common use case

This fitting is commonly used to refresh a subset of data while preserving historical records.

Pattern

Delete subset of data
→ Load refreshed data
→ Preserve remaining data

For example:

Delete Data:
academic_period = {{context.term_code}}

→ External Data (append)

Best practices

  • Use parameterized conditions instead of hard-coding values
  • Validate delete conditions before running in production
  • Set a reasonable Max Rows value to limit risk
  • Test with small datasets before running on large tables
  • Use with External Data fitting for incremental refresh patterns

Considerations

  • Incorrect conditions can result in unintended data deletion
  • Unresolved parameters may cause the delete operation to fail
  • Max Rows prevents large deletions but will cause the operation to fail if exceeded
External Data fitting

Insights External Data fitting formats a data stream into a delimited report, uploads to Data Lake, monitors the resulting transformation job, and returns the result of the job.

Note: Institutions should not use the External Data fitting in conjunction with Create Table fitting for the same table. They are independent fittings and will yield unexpected results if they are used together for the same table.

Also, the External Data fitting is only available for accounts with an Insights Enterprise Extensibility license.

Expected input

The fitting expects a stream of messages. Message payload can be an object or a string. The payloads of type object are formatted into csv and payloads of type string are uploaded to Data Lake directly with no formatting.

Expected configuration

Configuration Description
Data Source Name Required. The data source name.

This property supports parameterization using Mustache expression syntax (for example, {{context.dataSourceName}}). Values are resolved at pipeline runtime.
Dataset Template Name Required. The name of the dataset template.

This property supports parameterization using Mustache expression syntax (for example, {{context.dataSetTemplateName}}). Values are resolved at pipeline runtime.
Data is in CSV Format

Optional. If enabled, assume that a CSV file is provided through a payload and the detail object configuration is ignored.
Data will be appended

Optional: If enabled, the uploaded file will be appended to existing data.

If disabled (default), the uploaded file will replace existing data.

If any column (from the table) is deleted while appendMode is enabled, the column in the target table will show as NULL (column will not be deleted but marked as it is deleted).
Detail Required. It defines how to handle each message payload and how it is laid out on each detail row. If useCSVFile is set, this configuration is ignored.
Table Required. Table definition for the data to be stored.

Detail Definition

Property Description
Columns Required. List of detail column object definitions. The number of detail columns should match the number of table columns.

Detail column object definition

The columns configuration property accepts a list that contains string values. Sometimes property names do not make for good column headers, so the column object definition allows for a property path to be set along with a label.

For a column configuration:

Property Description
Path Required.
  • The path property allows for simple and nested object references.
  • A simple string value represents location (or path) within the message payload object where the column value is located.
  • If label is not provided, the very same value will be used as column header.
  • For flat objects, just the name of the property will suffice.
  • For complex objects with nested objects, the string can handle dot notation.
Label Optional. Label for the column.

Table Definition

Property Description
Table Name Required. Table name. Spaces and special characters are not supported in table name.

This property supports parameterization using Mustache expression syntax (for example, {{context.dataSetTemplateName}}). Values are resolved at pipeline runtime.
Table Description Optional. Table description.

This property supports parameterization using Mustache expression syntax (for example, {{context.dataSetTemplateName}}). Values are resolved at pipeline runtime.
Table Columns Required. List of table column object definitions. If detail is used, the number of table columns should match the number of detail columns.

Table column object definition

For a tableColumn configuration:

Property Description
Name

Required. The column name must be unique. When Data is in CSV Format is set to disabled, the value provided should match an existing detail column label.

If no label with a matching name is found a path with a matching value should be present.

Table column name should not contain spaces, special characters and cannot use mixed casing.

Do not use these reserved column names: dml_type, tenant_id, datasource_id, timestamp, last_updated_date.
Type Required. Data type of the column values. For example, varchar (length) where length is a positive integer, numeric, timestamp without timezone, etc.
Length Required if attribute type is varchar. Optional when attribute type is numeric or decimal.
Precision Optional. Can be set if attribute is numeric or decimal.
Scale Optional. Can be set if attribute is numeric or decimal.
Nullable Optional. Indicates whether a null data value is allowed in the associated column. defaults to disabled.

Parameterization Using Mustache Expressions

The following configuration properties support parameterization using Mustache template syntax:

  • Data Source Name
  • Dataset Template Name
  • Table Name
  • Table Description

Mustache expressions are evaluated at pipeline runtime using the standard interpolation context. Supported context objects include:

  • context — The pipeline execution context (including pipeline parameters)
  • message or msg — The first incoming message (header and payload)

This capability allows a single pipeline definition to be reused across multiple tenants, institutions, or data sources by supplying different parameter values at execution time.

If a configuration value does not contain a Mustache expression, the configured string is used as-is. Existing pipelines that use hard-coded values continue to function without modification.

Compatibility note

The Add Primary Key fitting is not supported in pipelines that use the External Data fitting.

The External Data fitting manages schema metadata and data submission for processing by Insights. Table structure and schema updates are controlled by Insights during transformation processing.

Supported data types

The following data types are supported. Data that is passed as input to each column with a specific type must follow format supported by Postgres. Links to supported formats are provided below.

  • Boolean - datatype-boolean
  • Date - datatype-datetime
  • Decimal - datatype-numeric
  • Numeric - datatype-numeric
  • Text - datatype-character
  • Time - datatype-datetime
  • Timestamp without timezone - datatype-datetime
  • Varchar - datatype-character

Output

This fitting pushes a message into the pipeline. The output payload is a JSON object. If the pipeline containing this fitting is executed in Test mode from Designer, transformation job is not invoked. Fitting will validate data that it receives and if data fails validation, errors display.

Example fitting executed successfully in Designer (Test mode):

{ 
  "response": "CSV Data validated successfully"
}

Example fitting executed with validation errors in Designer (Test mode):

[
    {
      "payload": {
        "response": "CSV Data validation failed with errors"
      },
    }
  ],
  "runId": "runId",
  "errors": [
    {
      "severity": "Error",
      "responseCode": 400,
      "description": "Validation error description",
      "correlationId": "runId",
      "request": {}
    }
  ]

Example fitting executed successfully in runtime UI:

{ 
  "response": {
    "id": "transformationJobId", 
    "name": "jobName", 
    "status": "completed", 
    "message": "1 of 1 Stage completed successfully.", 
    "correlationId": "correlationId
  }
}
Extract Data fitting

The Extract Data fitting enables Insights to serve as a source for Data Connect Integration Designer pipelines.

The Extract Data fitting requires Experience Premium and either Insights Foundation or Insights Premium licenses.

Pipeline parameters can be set for the Extract Data fitting. See the Parameters section in Develop pipelines for more information about setting pipeline parameters.

Expected input

A message payload that is a JavaScript object.

Expected configuration

{
  "pipelineName": "string", // required. Unique name of the pipeline (transformation).
  "segmentName": "string", // required. Unique name for segment (step).
  "class": "extractData", // required, enum.
  "config": {
    "selectQuery": "string", // required. SQL query that will be used to to create the extract.
    "bulkEnabled": "boolean" //required. Indicates that query results are extracted in a bulk optimized way on the backend.  Enabled by default.
  }
}
Configuration Description
Pipeline Name Required. Unique name of the pipeline.
Segment Name Required. Unique name for segment.
Class Required.
Select Query Required. SQL query that will be used to create the extract.
Bulk Enabled Required. Indicates that query results are extracted in a bulk optimized way on the back end.
Ignore Errors Optional. Flag to enable or disable error reporting to Ethos whenever an error is caught. Use this in conjunction with Error Path to implement custom error handling logic further in the pipeline.
Error Path Optional. Dot-notation error path. Setting this will push original message forward with error details. Error path can specify a location in header or payload.

Output

This fitting pushes a message into the pipeline for each row of data received from Insights. The output payload is a JSON object.

Following is an example of a successfully executed fitting:

{
    "data": [
        {
            "header": {},
            "payload": {
                "spriden_id": "375067745"
            },
            "__type": "ETHOS_MESSAGE"
        }
    ],
    "runId": "5927eab7-045b-4957-82f4-dae812cd4d45"
}

Parameterized Queries

To test a pipeline with the Extract Data fitting in the Data Connect Integration Designer, the user building the pipeline must have SQL Query Data permission. If the user does not have adequate permission, the Integration Designer displays an error when attempting to test the pipeline. See Data permissions for more information about SQL Query permission in Insights and how to enable it.

Using parameters

Parameters can be added to queries using Mustache syntax in the Select Query, as shown here: 

select * from stvterm
where stvterm_code = {{context.termCode}}

In the example above, the parameter value for context.termCode will be passed to the query at runtime.

In the case of a context parameter, the parameter is created in Pipeline Settings and can be set at runtime when testing in Integration Designer or when a job is created in Integration Packages.

In addition to context parameters, message parameters can be used by referencing a key in the message payload or header. For example:

...
where stvterm_code = {{message.payload.termCode}}

or

...
where stvterm_code = {{message.header.termCode}}

Strings, numbers, dates, and Boolean values can be passed to parameters.

It is easier to set date values using JavaScript than using the date picker in the Pipeline Settings user interface, because the date picker sets the time zone to the local time zone, and most database column values do not have a timestamp.

Example of setting the date and time using the JavaScript Transform fitting:

function transform (message, context) {
  // datetime in ISO 8601 format without timezone
  message.header.date_param = new Date('2024-01-08T15:18:05.000Z');
  return message;
}

Passing null values to parameters

Database null values can be passed to parameters with some limitations.

Passing null values through the context is limited to string parameters:

  • To pass a null to a string parameter, enter the value "null" (without double quotes).
  • To pass an empty string, enter two single quotes ('').

Null values can be passed to parameters using the JavaScript Transform fitting to set values in the message header and payload. Null values must be passed as an object that has the data type as the key. For example: {'string':null}.

Examples of how to pass null values using the JavaScript Transform fitting:

function transform (message, context) {
  // db null for a string parameter
  message.payload.null_string_param = {'string':null};
  // empty string for a string parameter 
  message.payload.empty_string_param = '';
  // db null for a number parameter 
  message.payload.null_number_param = {'number':null};
  // db null for a date parameter 
  message.header.null_date_param = {'date':null}
  // db null for a boolean parameter 
  message.header.null_boolean_param = {'boolean':null};
  return message;
}

See Example: Build a pipeline to extract Insights data and How to use parameters with Insights Custom Transformations fittings.

  // datetime in ISO 8601 format without timezone
  message.header.date_param = new Date('2024-01-08T15:18:05.000Z');
  return message;
}

Passing null values to parameters

Database null values can be passed to parameters with some limitations.

Passing null values through the context is limited to string parameters:

  • To pass a null to a string parameter, enter the value "null" (without double quotes).
  • To pass an empty string, enter two single quotes ('').

Null values can be passed to parameters using the JavaScript Transform fitting to set values in the message header and payload. Null values must be passed as an object that has the data type as the key. For example: {'string':null}.

Examples of how to pass null values using the JavaScript Transform fitting:

function transform (message, context) {
  // db null for a string parameter
  message.payload.null_string_param = {'string':null};
  // empty string for a string parameter 
  message.payload.empty_string_param = '';
  // db null for a number parameter 
  message.payload.null_number_param = {'number':null};
  // db null for a date parameter 
  message.header.null_date_param = {'date':null}
  // db null for a boolean parameter 
  message.header.null_boolean_param = {'boolean':null};
  return message;
}

Find an API with the API Selector

The API Selector provides an intuitive means to view and select data returned by an API, so that the data can be used in other applications.

About this task

With the API Selector, you can search for an API based on your existing knowledge about Ellucian APIs or the source systems that the APIs pull from.
The API Selector searches the following APIs:
  • The APIs delivered by Ellucian, including Colleague Ethos APIs, Banner Ethos APIs, Banner Business Process APIs, and other APIs exposed through Ellucian solutions. Your search is limited to APIs that are relevant to your implementation. For example, Colleague customers will not see Banner APIs in the search results.
  • Data Connect Serverless APIs developed for your institution.
  • APIs generated by Banner Custom Schemas for your institution.

Procedure

  1. Access the Search API Catalog page.
    • Open this page using a direct link from the application that will use the data. For example, that application might include a Select API link, or similar.
    • Open this page from the API Selector card on your Experience home page or dashboard. To open the Search API Catalog page from the card, click anywhere in the card, and then click the Search APIs button.
    Your institution must have enabled the API Selector card in Experience before you can access the card or the Search API Catalog page. If it has not enabled the card, you cannot access this card and will receive a HTTP 404 Page Not Found error if you attempt to open a link to the Search API Catalog page.
    If you have enabled the card, the Search API Catalog page appears when you click the link or the Search APIs button. The page contains a search field where you can search for Ellucian APIs, with a drop-down list that you can use to focus your search.
  2. In the drop-down list at the side of the search field, select a category to focus the search, or accept the default category (All) to search all categories.
    Category Description Example Search Query
    Name Name, description, or title of the API All or part of the name or title of the API, or a term in its description. For example, identity.
    Source Originating system of the API For example Banner, Colleague or CRM Advance.
    Database Object Data model or data source in the originating system The Banner or Colleague table or column name. For example, person.
    Response Property Name of a property that is returned by the API All or part of the name of a JSON property returned in the response payload. For example academicPrograms.
    Request Parameter Name of a parameter that the API accepts All or part of the name of a request parameter, that is the value of a name property in the request. For example, academicCatalog.
  3. In the search field, enter your search query.
    As you enter the query, the system dynamically updates a list of up to ten APIs that match the query, below the search field. You can now click one of these APIs (if the list contains the desired API) or press Enter to run the current query.
  4. Optional: If you see the desired API in the list, click the name of the API name to open the details page for that API.
    See Step 7.
  5. Optional: If you do not see the desired API in the list, press Enter to run the query.

    The system updates the page to display a list of results that contain summary information about the APIs that match the query. This list includes the Name column, which contains the name of the API that is also a link you can click to open the details page for that API.

    The system also displays a set of filters, above the results, that you can use to filter these results:
    • Statuses—The status of the API, GA (General Availability) for example.
    • Sources—The originating system of the API.
    • Domains—The API domain, for example Advancement.
    • Methods—The HTTP methods supported by the APIs in the result set.
    • Authorization Type—The authorization type of the APIs in the result set, for example Basic Auth.

    Each filter contains a list of values associated with the filter, and you can filter the search results by selecting the check box, or check box, for each value. The list for each filter only contains values that apply to the APIs returned by the current search query. If the query only returns a single value for a filter, the system deactivates that filter and displays the value in the list for it. For example, if your query only returns APIs that have a GA status, then it deactivates the Statuses filter and displays GA in the list.

  6. Optional: Filter the result set if required, locate your desired API, and click the link in the Name column for this API.
    The system opens the API details page for the API you selected.
  7. On the API details page, view detailed information about the API.

    The details page includes a Version list and the API Details section, at the side of the page. It also contains the Search API Catalog link, at the top of the page, which you can click to return to the Search API Catalog page.

    The main body of the details page displays the documentation for the API. The API Selector documents APIs using the industry standard OpenAPI definitions and displays these definitions using Swagger UI.

  8. In the Version list, select an option.
    Note: The API Selector selects the latest version in the Version list by default. Ellucian recommends that you use the latest version which contains the most up-to-date information. If the latest version does not have the fields that you need to interact with your source system, you can review other versions.
    When you select a version, the API Selector updates the information in the API Details section and the documentation in the main body of the page for the selected API version.
  9. For the API that you want to use in your application, click the link for the desired HTTP method.
    For example, click SELECT GET if your application requires the GET method. If there are multiple choices for the desired method, for example, multiple SELECT GET choices, choose the appropriate method based on the displayed path.
